title: Visits to US McDonald's locations falls as customers struggle with cost of living
summary: Traffic at U.S. McDonald’s restaurants fell during the third quarter as customers struggled with higher gas prices and the uncomfortably high cost of living
story: Traffic at U.S. McDonald’s restaurants fell during the third quarter as customers struggled with higher gas prices and the uncomfortably high cost of living
Traffic at U.S. McDonald’s restaurants fell during the third quarter as customers struggled with higher gas prices and the uncomfortably high cost of living.

U.S. same-store sales – or sales at locations open at least a year -- fell 0.2% in the July-September period, the Chicago burger giant said Wednesday. While that was not as bad as the 0.5% drop Wall Street had expected, it was the first retreat for McDonald's since early 2025.

McDonald’s restored in-app deals and its marketing was focused on value during the quarter, which helped push same-store sales into positive territory in September. But the shift in focus at McDonald’s shows how challenging the economic environment has become for U.S. fast food companies.
Third-quarter foot traffic fell 2.6% across the entire fast food sector in the U.S., according to Revenue Management Solutions, a restaurant industry consultant.

“This is the environment that we’re in right now. You have to be on your game and deliver that value,” said McDonald’s Chairman and CEO Chris Kempczinski during an investor presentation last month. “The pressure around cost of living isn’t going away.”

Globally, same-store sales rose 1.3% in the same period that U.S. sales fell. Strong sales in Germany and Australia helped offset weakness in France, which was rocked by protests that began in September.
Revenue rose 1% to $7.16 billion for the quarter, short of Wall Street expectations of $7.28 billion.
Net income rose 9% to $2.49 billion. Adjusted for one-time items, the company earned $3.57 per share. That beat analysts’ forecast for a $3.38 per-share profit.

title: New York's Strand Bookstore to repay nearly $1.5M after improperly receiving federal loan
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has announced that New York's Strand Bookstore will pay nearly $1.5 million after improperly receiving a pandemic-era small business loan
story: The U.S. Department of Justice has announced that New York's Strand Bookstore will pay nearly $1.5 million after improperly receiving a pandemic-era small business loan

NEW YORK -- New York's beloved Strand Bookstore will pay back nearly $1.5 million after improperly applying for and receiving a pandemic-era small business loan even though it wasn't eligible, the U.S. Department of Justice has announced.
According to the DOJ, the Strand was ineligible because the owner, Nancy Bass Wyden, is the wife of U.S. Sen. Ron Wyden, a Democrat from Oregon. The DOJ announced the settlement Tuesday.

In 2021, the Strand applied for a second draw loan of $932,350 from the Paycheck Protection Program, which required applicants to certify that a member of Congress did not have a direct or indirect controlling interest in the business. The bookstore had previously received a PPP loan in 2020, but that money did not require the same certification.

“The Paycheck Protection Program was created to save American jobs, not to enrich those who aren’t eligible for taxpayer-funded relief, especially the wife of a U.S. Senator,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro in a statement.

Bass Wyden said in a statement that during the COVID-19 pandemic, the laws and regulations surrounding government relief programs “were changing rapidly” and that the bookstore was not aware of the eligibility changes between when it applied for the first and second loan.

“We stand by the facts: the circumstances arose during an unprecedented and rapidly changing public health emergency, the mistake was unintentional, and the funds were returned as soon as the issue came to our attention,” Bass Wyden said. “We regret the oversight and recognize the importance of complying with all applicable laws and regulations.”

The Associated Press has sent an email requesting comment to the Strand. A spokesperson for Wyden's office said the senator and his wife do not discuss her business and he had no involvement in the loan or settlement.

Known for its “18 Miles of Books” on its shelves, the Strand is a fixture of New York’s cultural scene and downtown life. It has appeared in numerous TV shows and movies, including “Sex and the City,” “Julie & Julia,” “Six Degrees of Separation,” and more. Offerings range from used paperbacks for a few dollars apiece to rare first editions, and it is a prime spot for authors to give book talks.
Bass Wyden’s grandfather, Benjamin Bass, founded the shop in 1927. She and her father, Fred Bass, ran it together before his death in 2018.

After the coronavirus pandemic spurred lockdowns and upended brick-and-mortar businesses, Bass Wyden appealed to the public in October 2020 to shop at the Strand in person or online. She said in a social media post that “the loan we were given” had kept the store afloat for eight months, but revenues were down 70% and the business was “unsustainable.”
A #savethestrand campaign then brought in more than 25,000 online orders in one weekend, Bass Wyden told The Washington Post at the time.

According to the Post, Bass Wyden had furloughed 188 of 217 employees when lockdowns began in March 2020, brought back 30 workers that June after getting a Paycheck Protection Program loan of between $1 million and $2 million, but then laid off 12 workers some weeks later.
Meanwhile, strife mounted between her and the workers’ union, particularly after it emerged that she had bought at least $115,000 worth of Amazon stock during the pandemic.
___ Kruesi reported from Providence, Rhode Island.

title: 5 retired MLB umpires — including Joe West — sue benefit plan, alleging they are owed more money
summary: Five retired umpires have sued their retirement plan and its committee, claiming they are owed additional money
story: Five retired umpires have sued their retirement plan and its committee, claiming they are owed additional money
NEW YORK -- Five retired umpires have sued their retirement plan from their work for Major League Baseball and the plan's retirement committee, alleging they are owed additional money.
Joe West, Tom Hallion, Gerry Davis, Larry Vanover and Jerry Layne filed the lawsuit on Sept. 29 in federal court in New York.

They claimed their benefits were not correctly calculated and alleged they should receive additional money under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. Their lawyer, Paul B. Holmes, said Thursday the amount owed the five is in excess of $5 million.

West said that when he brought up the issue to the retirement committee, he was offered a relatively small sum. West said MLB senior vice president and chief employment counsel Steven Gonzalez told him: “If you don't like the number, sue us.”
“Does Steve Gonzalez not know my history with dealing with lawsuits?” West said.
West, who worked a record 5,460 regular-season games from 1976-2021, was awarded $500,000 in damages in 2021 for a defamation suit against former All-Star catcher Paul LoDuca.
MLB declined comment Wednesday, citing the pending lawsuit. The suit was first reported by USA Today.

West and Davis retired after the 2021 season, Hallion after 2022, and Layne and Vanover at the end of 2024. The suit was filed against the American Leagues and National Leagues of Professional Baseball Clubs Retirement Income Plan for Umpires and that entity's retirement committee.

“In some of the issues you could argue it both ways, but in a couple of the issues it was pretty clear that they were just shorting the umpires,” Holmes said. “And so we went through the process and we went through settlement talks. I think these guys were willing to take something less than 100% of what we thought they were entitled to just to avoid litigation and be done with it, but MLB’s offers were not very competitive.”
These umpires sued as individuals. The Major League Baseball Umpires Association is not a party.
“The union wanted to stay out of it,” Holmes said. “It's not a big union and they're not pension experts.”
U.S. District Judge Ronnie Abrams scheduled a pretrial conference for Dec. 11.

title: UK will face AI cyberattacks on critical infrastructure by 2028, official says
summary: Britain’s cyberchief says the U.K. is likely to face artificial intelligence cyberattacks on its critical infrastructure by 2028
story: Britain’s cyberchief says the U.K. is likely to face artificial intelligence cyberattacks on its critical infrastructure by 2028

LONDON -- The United Kingdom will likely face artificial intelligence cyberattacks on its critical infrastructure by 2028 as criminals and states, including China and Russia, increasingly use AI in their cyberactivity, Britain's cyberchief said Tuesday.

That could include AI-powered malware for ransomware attacks as the technology will allow “vulnerabilities that have been tolerated for far too long” to be discovered and exploited “at a scale that was once unimaginable,” said Richard Horne, the head of the National Cyber Security Center.
One such vulnerability was discovered in refrigeration units that were targeted by hackers who turned up the temperature, causing food to thaw. The U.K. has also been affected, Horne said.

In a speech marking the publication of the annual cyber report by the National Cyber Security Center, or NCSC, Horne said that the leaders of businesses and organizations of all sizes who have “got away with tech on the cheap” will have to explain why “food isn't on the shelves, lights aren't on, businesses have gone under,” if they fail to invest in cybersecurity or update out-of-date technology.

Chinese cyberactivity is the “most sophisticated and sustained cyber challenge facing the U.K.” while both Russia and China will routinely use AI to achieve their geopolitical goals, the report said. Russia is intentionally conducting cybercampaigns which fall below the threshold of armed conflict, while Iran is carrying out attacks against the U.K. and targeting individuals who are a threat to the Iranian government, Horne said.

The use of AI by states and criminals is highly likely to increase the scale and efficiency of hostile operations, but AI is more likely to be used to enhance and scale existing tactics and techniques rather than find brand new vulnerabilities, the report said.

Technology “underpins the automation of physical processes that are vital to modern life,” Horne said. That includes, he said, electricity switching, sluice gates in water facilities, dam operations, manufacturing lines, heating and refrigeration controls. The recent cyberattacks on refrigeration systems in French supermarkets showed how easily hostile actors could exploit civilian infrastructure, Horne said.

Fridges across Europe have been affected, including in the U.K., where security experts from the NCSC worked “through the night” to contact organizations with the vulnerable technology, Horne told The Associated Press.

Refrigeration systems in France were attacked because they were using old technology which was no longer being updated and that was connected directly to the internet with default passwords, Horne said. It was, he said, not an AI attack but one where bad actors exploited vulnerabilities that have existed for a long time and showed the need for businesses to address the security of operational technology.

Last week, governments and corporations worked on urgent security updates after the AI-assisted discovery of vulnerabilities in a programming language vital to 70% of websites globally. The two critical flaws identified by AI could allow bad actors to get unauthenticated access to sites which, in theory, could allow them to control a web server remotely without needing a password.

Russia has already attacked critical infrastructure in Europe, according to the U.K. and European Union member states that said Russia's FSB security service was behind an attack on Poland's energy grid in December 2025. If the attack had been successful, 500,000 people could have lost electricity during winter.

In the U.K., malicious cyberactivity is costing organizations almost $20 billion every year, the NCSC said. In 2025, the carmaker Jaguar Land Rover suffered more than $260 million in direct losses following a cyberattack which also hit suppliers and dented the U.K. economy.

“We need every organization in the U.K. to take action now. Not only to protect their customers, services and livelihoods, but because cybersecurity is now part of the front-line defense of our nation,” said Anne Keast-Butler, director of GCHQ, Britain’s signals intelligence agency, which the NCSC is part of.

That includes implementing basic but effective cybersecurity measures such as making sure devices are up to date, limiting administrator access to systems and backing up important files and data, the NCSC said.

title: Belarus hosts trans-Atlantic security group's chief, part of efforts to improve ties with the West
summary: The chief of a top trans-Atlantic security grouping has visited Belarus for the first time in years
story: The chief of a top trans-Atlantic security grouping has visited Belarus for the first time in years

TALLINN, Estonia -- The chief of a top trans-Atlantic security grouping visited Belarus on Tuesday for the first time in seven years as the country’s authoritarian President Alexander Lukashenko has sought to normalize ties with the West.

Feridun Sinirlioglu, the secretary-general of the Vienna-based Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, visited Belarus to attend an international security conference and met with Lukashenko.
Sinirlioglu’s visit to Belarus marks the first such trip by the OSCE’s chief since 2019. Belarus, a close ally of Russia, has faced Western isolation and sanctions for years.
Speaking at the start of his meeting with Lukashenko, Sinirlioglu noted Belarus’ role in helping organize exchanges of prisoners of war between Russia and Ukraine.

The Belarusian leader said that he “highly appreciates” Sinirlioglu's visit, but he also criticized the OSCE for what he described as its purported pro-Western stance and unfair criticism of elections in Belarus and Russia.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov attended the conference along with diplomats from ex-Soviet nations, China and other countries.

Lukashenko has governed the nation of 9.5 million with an iron fist for more than three decades, and Belarus has been sanctioned repeatedly by Western countries — both for its crackdown on human rights and for allowing Moscow to use its territory in the full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022.

Belarusian opposition leader-in-exile Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya said that “for Lukashenko, a meeting with the OSCE's secretary-general is already a significant and entirely undeserved political reward.”
“High-level visits and meetings with Lukashenko — if they don't lead to concrete changes — only strengthen his regime and foster a sense of impunity,” Tsikhanouskaya told The Associated Press.

“Engagement must yield real results — the release of political prisoners, an end to repression, and a withdrawal of support for the Russian aggression — rather than serving as a tool to grant the regime international legitimacy,” she said.

Lukashenko’s rule was challenged after a 2020 presidential election that kept him in power, when tens of thousands of people poured into the streets to protest a vote widely seen as rigged. In an ensuing crackdown, tens of thousands of people were detained, with many beaten by police. Prominent opposition figures either fled the country or were imprisoned.

Since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to the White House for his second term, Lukashenko has released hundreds of political prisoners in a series of U.S.-mediated deals that also lifted some U.S. sanctions, part of his efforts to overcome isolation and normalize ties with the West.

As part of a deal in March that Washington helped broker, Lukashenko ordered the release of 250 political prisoners, while the U.S. agreed to lift sanctions on two Belarusian state banks and the country’s Finance Ministry, and to remove the top Belarusian potash producers from a sanctions list. And in September, Belarusian authorities released 25 prisoners in exchange for the lifting of U.S. sanctions against two Belarusian companies.
The Belarusian opposition has welcomed the prisoners’ release, but noted that many others remain in custody. Belarus still has 887 political prisoners, according to the Viasna human rights center.

title: Ryanair CEO anticipates European airfare prices up as much as 20% next year
summary: The CEO for Ryanair expects European airfare prices may climb as much as 20% next year as jet fuel prices rise
story: The CEO for Ryanair expects European airfare prices may climb as much as 20% next year as jet fuel prices rise
The CEO for Ryanair expects European plane ticket prices may climb as much as 20% next year with the conflict in the Middle East ongoing.
“So we’re facing 2027 where we have much higher oil prices... I think they’re going to get passed on in significantly higher airfares,” CEO Michael O’Leary said in a Monday interview on CNBC.
The price of jet fuel has been extremely volatile after the U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran.

Jet fuel has risen even faster than oil during the war, reflecting both higher crude prices and tight supplies of the refined fuel that is one of the largest operating expenses for airlines. Carriers have cut some less profitable flights and raised fares and baggage fees, although major U.S. airlines said higher passenger revenue initially covered only part of their soaring fuel costs.

Globally, jet fuel averaged about $99 a barrel on Feb. 27, the day before the war began, according to the International Air Transport Association’s Jet Fuel Price Monitor. Prices more than doubled to $209 by early April, fell for nearly three months and reached $195 a barrel in mid-September following their renewed ascent, IATA said, citing data from S&P Global Energy Platts. The global average jet fuel price is currently hovering around $196 a barrel.
Since diesel and jet fuel are closely related products that compete for space at refineries, shortages of one can put additional pressure on the price and availability of the other.
The IATA expects fuel to account for nearly one-third of airline operating expenses this year, up from about a quarter in 2025.

Ryanair said Monday that it doesn't expect European short haul airfares to fully offset anticipated increases in its fuel bill for next year, so it is reviewing its costs and may have to impose temporary pay freezes, lower crew ratios and use more artificial intelligence to get further productivity for back office and support functions.

title: KFC, Taco Bell locations close across Puerto Rico as they seek new franchise partner
summary: All KFC and Taco Bell restaurants in Puerto Rico have temporarily closed after Yum
story: All KFC and Taco Bell restaurants in Puerto Rico have temporarily closed after Yum

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico -- All KFC and Taco Bell restaurants in Puerto Rico have temporarily closed after parent company Yum! Brands ended its relationship with an island-based operator, officials said Monday.
Kentucky-based Yum! Brands said it made the “difficult decision to end its relationship" with Encanto Restaurants because that company "can no longer operate in a way that meets our standards.”
“We remain deeply committed to Puerto Rico and are working as quickly as possible to welcome customers back to our restaurants,” Yum! Brands said in a statement shared with The Associated Press.
KFC Puerto Rico and Taco Bell Puerto Rico posted brief statements saying they are working to find a new franchise partner.
“We hope to be able to serve you again very soon,” KFC Puerto Rico wrote on Instagram.
Encanto Restaurants did not immediately return a message seeking comment.
Puerto Rico’s first KFC restaurant opened in 1967, while Encanto Restaurants began operating Taco Bell in 1985, according to the company.
Encanto Restaurants also operates Pizza Hut and IHOP restaurants in the U.S. territory. Overall, it operates 180 restaurants on the island and employs more than 3,000 people.

title: Dodge announces return to NASCAR Cup Series beginning at Daytona 500
summary: Dodge is returning to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, a year earlier than initially expected
story: Dodge is returning to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, a year earlier than initially expected
LAS VEGAS -- Dodge is returning to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, a year earlier than initially expected.
The Stellantis-owned Dodge brand announced its return at the SEMA Show in Las Vegas on Monday.

Dodge will once again give the Cup Series four manufacturers, joining Chevrolet, Ford and Toyota in fielding entries to compete in a 36-race schedule that begins in mid-February and crowns a champion in early November.
Kaulig Racing will use the Dodge Charger to field a two-car team beginning at the Daytona 500. AJ Allmendinger and Ty Dillon are expected to fill those seats.

“Dodge’s return to the NASCAR Cup Series is a significant milestone for the sport,” NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell said in a statement. “This commitment speaks to Dodge’s belief in our sport and gives fans another reason to be excited about what’s ahead.

“The partnership between NASCAR, (Ram CEO) Tim Kuniskis and the entire team at Stellantis has been nothing short of phenomenal. They have a deep passion for NASCAR and its ability to showcase the world’s top brands, and we can’t wait to see Dodge on the racetrack for the Daytona 500 and beyond.”

Dodge raced in NASCAR through the 2012 season and left the same month it celebrated the Cup title with Brad Keselowski and Penske Racing. It was Dodge’s first Cup championship since Richard Petty’s sixth of seven titles in 1975.
Dodge re-entered the NASCAR Truck Series with its Ram brand in 2026, with eyes on expanding to the premier Cup Series in 2028. Kuniskis vowed to be disruptive while doing it “unlike anyone else.”

Kuniskis said Ram planned to tap into NASCAR’s estimated fan base of 20 million “and turn it into 80 or 100 million.” Kaulig had five trucks race this season, all of which are outside the top 10 in the series standings heading to the season finale at Homestead, Florida, this weekend.

Normally, it would have taken Dodge two years to get ready for the Cup Series. But Dodge bypassed part of the timeline required to develop a new engine by partnering with Earnhardt Childress Racing to build Dodge-spec powerplants alongside its regular Chevrolet operations.
Chevrolet, Ford and Toyota allowed that unique partnership in part because they believed a fourth manufacturer in NASCAR would be good for the overall health of the racing series.

title: Approval of cheap version of HIV-prevention shot raises hopes in low-income countries
summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a generic version of the world’s only twice-a-year shot to prevent HIV
story: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a generic version of the world’s only twice-a-year shot to prevent HIV

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a generic version of the world’s only twice-a-year shot to prevent HIV — a big step toward making the drug available inexpensively and more quickly in 120 low- and middle-income countries.
The announcement was made on Monday morning by the manufacturer and organizations that helped to speed up development of the medication, called lenacapavir.

The drug is expected to cost $40 a year per person in the countries where it will be available, the same price as daily preventive pills available now. But the shots are much more convenient than the pills because they’re needed much less frequently and they nearly eliminated new infections in two groundbreaking studies of people at high risk.

People don’t always take their daily dose of medication, “and if you do not take it, you cannot get protected against HIV,” said Carmen Pérez Casas, HIV lead for the grant-making organization Unitaid, a global health agency. “With lenacapavir, we are much more hopeful.”

Ultimately, advocates said, the medication should help drive down cases of HIV and AIDS — and deaths. According to the World Health Organization, 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV and 570,000 died from HIV-related causes last year.

With an affordable, high-quality generic medication now available, “we could help to scale this to the 20 million people around the world who need PrEP,” prescription medicine taken by people at risk of HIV before being exposed to the virus, said Carolyn Amole, who leads the HIV program for the Clinton Health Access Initiative, a global health organization.
“And if we scale to those levels,” she added, “we can actually begin to bring an end to the HIV epidemic.”

Generic lenacapavir can’t be sold in the U.S. because a brand-name version, Yeztugo, made by Gilead Sciences and approved last year, is still protected by a patent. The U.S. list price for that version, meaning the cost before insurance, is $28,218 a year. Gilead officials say that’s similar to some other types of PrEP, which stands for pre-exposure prophylaxis.

The new generic was approved by the FDA under a longstanding practice designed to ensure the quality of HIV-related drugs provided to other countries by the U.S. government. Approval of a drug by the U.S. FDA can speed regulatory approval in many other countries. The approval is considered “tentative,” the FDA's standard designation for generics while the originator remains under patent.

Until now, Gilead has been the sole supplier of lenacapavir, and demand has outstripped supply in low- and middle-income countries. Last year, Gilead established royalty-free licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers to enable production. Those voluntary licenses cover a specific set of countries in sub-Saharan Africa, Asia and Latin America.

“We share the sense of urgency around expanding access to lenacapavir for HIV prevention,” a Gilead spokesperson said in a statement. “We believe we have enabled the fastest and most sustainable path to expanding access for communities most affected by HIV.”

The generic was developed by India-based Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories under an agreement brokered by Unitaid, the Clinton Health Access Initiative and Wits RHI, a health research institute in Africa. The partners sought to accelerate development and make the drug available at an affordable price.

Common side effects with lenacapavir include injection site reactions, headache and nausea. People also must be tested for HIV prior to starting the drug and with each injection; drug-resistant HIV has been identified when used by people with an undiagnosed HIV infection.

“For any kind of PrEP … you need to have HIV testing in advance,” said Saiqa Mullick, director of implementation science with Wits RHI. “For many of the low- and middle-income countries, that is a rapid test.”

Generic lenacapavir should start to become available in some places within weeks, those helping with the effort said, although it could take a bit longer in countries that require the drug to go through their own approval processes before people can start taking it. Generic versions made by the other manufacturers have yet to be approved by FDA.

“The work is not done. Now, we need the funding to actually buy it for everyone who needs it and then we need to do the hard work of getting it to the millions of people who need it and want it,” Amole said. “But this is a great milestone.”
Casas said she’s optimistic that scientific advances — along with political will and funding — can help the world curb HIV.
“Now,” she said, “we have the tools.”
Gerald Imray in Cape Town, South Africa, contributed to this story.

title: Russian strikes choke Ukraine’s economy as steel shuts down and grain exports stall
summary: Ukraine's economy is struggling as Russia's air war targets industries, logistics networks and ports needed for exports
story: Ukraine's economy is struggling as Russia's air war targets industries, logistics networks and ports needed for exports

KAMIANSKE, Ukraine -- The furnaces are cold, the factory floor deserted, and twisted metal litters the grounds of Kamet Steel, a vast industrial complex that once helped power Ukraine’s economy but closed after a Russian attack.
Across the country, grain — a key export — piles up in fields and silos as farmers struggle to find routes safe from airstrikes and wait for prices to rise.

Russia’s intensified air campaign is slowly strangling Ukraine’s economy, targeting industrial and energy plants and the logistics networks, railways and export routes that keep it afloat. The near-daily strikes with ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones disrupt production and drive up transport costs.

As a result, Ukraine’s government faces a deepening cash crunch as the air war chokes its revenue from steel, agriculture and other key sources. The damage ripples across interconnected sectors just as Kyiv faces uncertainty over future U.S. support.

Ukraine’s central bank last week forecast a 0.4% economic contraction in 2026, reversing its previous projection of 1.8% growth, due to the attacks and a surge in global energy prices. Gov. Andriy Pyshnyy said the bank had also raised its inflation forecast to 12.5%, from 10% in July.

Ukraine spends some 40% of its gross domestic product on defense — far beyond what it can cover alone, notes Torbjörn Becker, director of the Stockholm Institute of Transition Economics. Raising taxes only would bring in a fraction of what is needed.
Missile strikes have halted steel production across Metinvest Group, the country’s mining and metals giant.

Kamet Steel, in the industrial city of Kamianske, accounted for more than a quarter of Ukraine’s steel output in 2025. The complex employed thousands producing steel and pig iron for domestic construction. It also supplied semi-finished steel to Metinvest’s facility in Bulgaria for the market there and elsewhere in Europe.
But five ballistic missiles struck the site on Sept. 5. Its closure has hurt Ukraine’s industrial economy, affecting construction, mining, engineering, energy and logistics.

Ukrzaliznytsia, the national railway operator, relies heavily on steel transport and other freight revenue. Businesses that rely on the plant could lose jobs and face bankruptcy, said Oleksandr Tretyakov, Kamet Steel’s CEO. European Union trade restrictions could hinder recovery by narrowing the market for Ukrainian steel exports, he said.
“This is the worst situation since the Second World War,” Tretyakov said, noting that steel once accounted for about 6% of Ukraine’s GDP.
“It did,” he said. “Right now, it’s zero.”
Agriculture accounts for up to 60% of Ukraine’s foreign currency earnings, making it critical to the wartime economy.
But Russian attacks on Black Sea shipping have sharply reduced traffic through Ukraine’s deep-water ports just as farmers need cash to prepare for the next planting season.

Ukraine’s Black Sea trade has collapsed with attacks on ports, vessels and logistics infrastructure, according to maritime data and analytics company Lloyd’s List Intelligence. There were only 21 ship arrivals at Black Sea ports in August, down about 90% from a year earlier.
Soaring insurance premiums and the constant threat of Russian strikes deter shipowners. Dozens of sailors have been killed in attacks this year.

“All our developments and all the innovations we achieved will be crossed out by this situation and we will need to start from zero later,” said Volodymyr Scavinskyi, trade director at Nibulon, one of Ukraine’s leading agricultural exporters.

Ship traffic from Ukraine's lower-capacity ports on the Danube River to the Black Sea has surged, even under the threat of Russian bombardment. But it is costly. The Danube delta's Sulina Channel is too shallow for the largest vessels, and dozens of ships often wait days to enter or leave the river.

Record low Danube water levels due to drought also constrain the route. Barges that once carried 1,500 tons are loading only 800 to 900 tons, Scavinskyi said. Nearly twice as many barges are needed to move the same volume, raising costs. Transporting each ton of corn from central Ukraine to Spain cost up to $50 earlier this year. Now, it can reach $150, he said.
“It’s still risky and you don’t have any guarantees that your voyage will be successful,” Scavinskyi said.
For Olena Shelest, commercial director at HarvEast, a major agricultural holding, the immediate challenge is finding buyers.

HarvEast is holding wheat in enormous silo bags, waiting for market prices to stabilize. But the grain must be sold by year's end to free up cash for next year’s planting. The company risks running out of money to sow the next crop, turning today’s export bottleneck into next year’s production crisis.
Corn prices have fallen sharply, from an average of $210 to $230 per ton last year to around $130, further squeezing farmers, Shelest said.

About 60% of HarvEast's sales used to go through Black Sea ports. The Danube ports of Reni and Izmail can handle only about 15% to 20% of overall national export volumes, Shelest said. Land routes through Poland and elsewhere in Europe offer alternatives but have higher transport costs.
The pressure is forcing farmers to cut spending on seeds and fertilizer, risking future yields.

Roksolana Pidlasa, head of the parliament’s budget committee, said Ukraine is facing its worst cash squeeze since Russia's 2022 invasion. Falling tax revenues have left the treasury struggling to cover planned spending despite international funding commitments.

Ukraine faces a gap of just under $25 billion in funding for 2026, with dozens of bills tied to international commitments requiring parliamentary approval by the end of the year. In 2027, the gap is expected to reach about $32.6 billion, plus around $45 billion for in-kind military support.

The loss of U.S. budget support has compounded the pressure. Washington provided $50 billion in purely budget support under President Joe Biden between 2022 and 2024, helping fund teachers and doctors’ salaries and pensions, according to the U.S. Government Accountability Office.

Since President Donald Trump returned to office, there has been no authorization of significant aid to Ukraine. Some aid appropriated under the Biden Administration is still in the pipeline, though the Trump administration has temporarily paused some deliveries, according to the Council on Foreign Relations.

Europe has become Ukraine’s largest source of overall support, providing 137 billion euros ($153 billion) in financial, humanitarian and military aid since the start of the war, compared with 115 billion euros ($129 billion) from the U.S., according to the Kiel Institute for the World Economy.
Defense, public sector salaries, pensions and social assistance take priority. The government has postponed construction, reconstruction and some winter preparation projects.
If Ukraine doesn't find a way to cover the deficit next year, “it will mean that we will not be able to pay teachers and doctors’ salaries and maintain hospitals,” Pidlasa said.
Associated Press Business Writer David McHugh in Frankfurt, Germany, and AP journalist Volodymyr Yurchuk in Kyiv contributed to this report.

title: Higher oil prices boost Saudi Aramco profits despite disruption from attacks
summary: Saudi Aramco is reporting a 35% increase in third-quarter net profit, boosted by higher oil prices and the sale of a stake in a Malaysian company
story: Saudi Aramco is reporting a 35% increase in third-quarter net profit, boosted by higher oil prices and the sale of a stake in a Malaysian company

FRANKFURT, Germany -- Majority state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco on Tuesday reported a 35% increase in third-quarter net profit as earnings were boosted by higher oil prices and the sale of its stake in a Malaysian refining and petrochemical company.

Net profit rose to $36.3 billion from $26.9 billion in the year-earlier quarter. Adjusted net profit, which leaves out the sale of a stake in PRefChem to Malaysian state oil company Petronas, rose 9% to $31.2 billion.
The company also benefitted from high profit margins at its refineries turning crude into useable products such as diesel fuel.

Saudi Aramco sold its oil for an average of $95.20 a barrel during the quarter, compared to $70.10 in the year-before quarter, the company said in a news release. Oil prices surged after the outbreak of the Iran war due to disruption of supply and uncertainty about the course of the conflict.

After the war began in February, Saudi Aramco was able to use its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu to maintain a significant share of its oil exports despite disruption of tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz due to the risk of Iranian attack. The pipeline was attacked Sept. 10 but has resumed flows.

Saudi oil is now also being transported through the strait using a U.S.-protected corridor near the coast of Oman. Exports have continued despite attacks on Aramco facilities by Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.
The company is a major source of revenue for the Saudi government as it invests in projects aimed at diversifying its economy.

title: Owner of private Serbian bank detained and accused of siphoning money
summary: Serbian authorities have detained the owner of a private bank on suspicion he was siphoning money from the lender
story: Serbian authorities have detained the owner of a private bank on suspicion he was siphoning money from the lender

BELGRADE, Serbia -- BELGRADE, Serbia (AP) — Serbian authorities Monday detained the owner of a private bank on suspicion he was siphoning money from the lender that was used for some public utility payments during the previous government of former President Aleksandar Vucic.

Alta Bank rose to prominence under the rule of Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party that was ousted from power in a parliamentary election last week. The bank has handled all electricity payments by millions of users in the capital Belgrade, as well as public parking accounts.

On Saturday, Serbia’s Central Bank revoked Alta Bank’s operating license and launched bankruptcy proceedings to protect the bank’s depositors, saying that its liquidity “has deteriorated significantly” and “could worsen further."
Serbia’s Deposit Insurance Agency, which guarantees deposits of up to 50,000 euros ($56,000), will act as Alta Bank's bankruptcy administrator, the central bank said.
Davor Macura, the bank owner who initially owned an exchange office before becoming a prominent banker, was given a 48-hour detention on Monday, prosecutors said.

Macura’s lawyers told local media he was present at the bank headquarters in Belgrade and fully cooperated during an hourslong police search over the weekend. Lawyers added that Macura will be questioned by the public prosecutor on Tuesday.

Macura, whose businesses also span retail and construction, is suspected of illegally moving 45 billion dinars ($428 million) out of Alta Bank’s vault. Two other persons were also held for aiding and abetting the crime.

The moves against Alta Bank and its owner came as part of a wave of changes triggered by Vucic’s defeat in the Oct. 25 election that also included resignations in the state-run media, arrests of several officials and an announced review of long-standing corruption cases.

Former central bank governor Kori Udovicki on Sunday criticized the Serbian Central Bank moves as too slow. She said on RTS television that the central bank “lost a week in which it could have limited the bank’s ability to transfer the money abroad or to the connected individuals.”

Alta Bank is a rare Serbian lender that allowed tens of thousands of Russian émigrés to open personal and business accounts. Scores of Russians have moved to Russia-friendly Serbia since the start of the invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Alta Bank's troubles resonated outside Serbia. The Central Bank of North Macedonia put Alta Bank’s subsidiary into temporary administration and limited cash withdrawals to 160 euros ($179) per week, while Montenegro's banking regulator shut down payment processing company Alta Pay.
In Serbia, armed police could be seen guarding the bank's offices in Belgrade after dozens of customers stood in long lines over the weekend trying to withdraw their savings.

Serbian investigative outlets in the past have described Macura as a tycoon whose political connections to Vucic and his SNS helped him win lucrative contracts with state agencies and public enterprises.

In 2024, Macura’s Alta Group came under scrutiny by the European Central Bank, or ECB, when it attempted to acquire a 20% stake in Austria’s Addiko Group through two connected firms to avoid triggering the ECB’s approval requirement. The ECB spotted this and stopped the deal. It also questioned the anti-money laundering controls and the source of funds in Macura's network.
The Association of Serbian Banks called Alta Bank's collapse “an individual issue” and said it would not affect other banks.

The SNS, which has governed Serbia since 2012, lost the parliamentary election to the student-led Student List movement. The outgoing authorities remain in control until a formal transition of power, expected to take several weeks.

Critics say the SNS has steadily taken control of state institutions since it came to power. It has been accused of corruption, cronyism, links to organized crime and pressure on the judiciary, police and media. The party has denied the accusations.

title: US job postings jumped sharply in September, a sign hiring could pick up
summary: U.S. employers ramped up their job postings in September as stronger economic growth may be encouraging more hiring
story: U.S. employers ramped up their job postings in September as stronger economic growth may be encouraging more hiring

WASHINGTON -- U.S. employers ramped up their job postings in September as stronger economic growth may be encouraging more hiring. Yet voters are headed to the polls Tuesday largely gloomy over an economy beset by higher prices.

U.S. job openings jumped to 7.5 million from a revised 7.19 million in August, the Labor Department reported Tuesday. It is the largest number of openings since May and up from a recent low of 6.9 million in March.
The department’s Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) also showed that gross hiring — job gains before subtracting people who quit or lost jobs — rose and layoffs fell in September.

The increases are a hopeful sign that hiring could improve, but the trend would have to continue for several months to suggest real improvement. Hiring has been sluggish for nearly three years, though layoffs have also been historically low, a sign of meager “churn” in the labor market. Low churn means those who are employed are enjoying relatively high levels of job security, but it is much harder than normal for those looking for work to find a job.

The government will issue the October jobs report on Friday, which is forecast to show that employers added 65,000 positions last month, according to data provider FactSet. That would be an improvement from 29,000 in September. The unemployment rate is expected to stay at a low 4.2%.

Typically, job gains of just 65,000 would be seen as a sign of a struggling economy, but with the giant baby boom generation retiring and immigration sharply reduced, the economy doesn’t need to generate as many jobs as it has in the past for unemployment to remain low.

In September, layoffs fell sharply to just 1.64 million, the fewest since March 2025. The number of people quitting their jobs rose to 3.37 million, the highest in about 18 months, and up from 3.04 million.
The rise in quits is generally a good sign because workers usually leave a job when they either have another lined up or when they are confident they can find new work.

title: Predators play the Avalanche, look to stop road losing streak
summary: The Nashville Predators hit the road against the Colorado Avalanche looking to end a three-game road skid
story: The Nashville Predators hit the road against the Colorado Avalanche looking to end a three-game road skid
Nashville Predators (6-4-5, in the Central Division) vs. Colorado Avalanche (9-6-1, in the Central Division)
Denver; Thursday, 9:30 p.m. EST
BOTTOM LINE: The Nashville Predators will try to break their three-game road losing streak in a matchup against the Colorado Avalanche.
Colorado is 9-6-1 overall and 3-2-1 against the Central Division. The Avalanche have allowed 52 goals while scoring 66 for a +14 scoring differential.
Nashville is 6-4-5 overall and 3-1-0 against the Central Division. The Predators are 1-1-1 when they commit more penalties than their opponent.
Thursday's game is the second time these teams meet this season. The Predators won 6-2 in the previous meeting. Ryan O'Reilly led the Predators with two goals.
TOP PERFORMERS: Martin Necas has seven goals and 11 assists for the Avalanche. Artturi Lehkonen has eight goals and four assists over the past 10 games.
Filip Forsberg has five goals and 14 assists for the Predators. O'Reilly has scored six goals and added six assists over the past 10 games.
LAST 10 GAMES: Avalanche: 5-4-1, averaging 3.7 goals, seven assists, 3.6 penalties and 7.5 penalty minutes while giving up 3.2 goals per game.
Predators: 4-3-3, averaging 3.1 goals, 5.3 assists, 3.3 penalties and 7.2 penalty minutes while giving up 3.2 goals per game.
INJURIES: Avalanche: Zachary L'Heureux: out (upper body), Josh Manson: out (lower body).
Predators: Jonathan Marchessault: day to day (undisclosed), William Trudeau: out (upper body).

title: Glover-Toscano scores 22 points as Saint Joseph’s defeats Longwood 82-73
summary: Saint Joseph defeats Longwood 82-73 on Wednesday, led by Jaiden Glover-Toscano's 22 points
story: Saint Joseph defeats Longwood 82-73 on Wednesday, led by Jaiden Glover-Toscano's 22 points
PHILADELPHIA -- Jaiden Glover-Toscano scored 15 of his 22 points in the second half to lead Saint Joseph's to an 82-73 victory over Longwood on Wednesday.
Glover-Toscano added seven rebounds for the Hawks (1-0). Khaafiq Myers scored 17 points and added six rebounds. BJ Ranson had 17 points and shot 6 for 13, including 3 for 6 from beyond the arc.
Alphonzo Billups III led the way for the Lancers (1-1) with 17 points. Longwood got 14 points from M.J. Williams. Jaylen Benard finished with 13 points, 10 rebounds and two steals.
Saint Joseph’s took the lead with 9:41 remaining in the first half and did not trail again. Ranson led the Hawks with eight points in the first half to help put them ahead 40-28 at the break.
Up next
Both teams next play Saturday. Saint Joseph’s (PA) hosts Lafayette and Longwood plays North Carolina Central at home.

title: Pagotto’s 30 lead Northern Kentucky past South Dakota 102-94
summary: Noah Pagotto scores 30 points as Northern Kentucky beats South Dakota 102-94
story: Noah Pagotto scores 30 points as Northern Kentucky beats South Dakota 102-94
VERMILLION, S.D. -- Noah Pagotto put up 30 points as Northern Kentucky beat South Dakota 102-94 on Wednesday.

Pagotto shot 11 of 15 from the field and 7 for 11 from the line for the Norse (2-0). Willie Foster scored 22 points while going 7 of 14 from the floor, including 3 for 5 from 3-point range, and 5 for 5 from the line. Eric Acker also had 22 points and shot 7 for 13 (2 for 3 from 3-point range) and 6 of 9 from the free-throw line.

title: Dosunmu scores 21 and Kuminga sparks late surge in Timberwolves’ 117-107 win over Rockets
summary: Ayo Dosunmu had 21 points and Jonathan Kuminga powered a fourth-quarter run that allowed the Minnesota Timberwolves to pull away for a 117-107 win over the Houston Rockets
story: Ayo Dosunmu had 21 points and Jonathan Kuminga powered a fourth-quarter run that allowed the Minnesota Timberwolves to pull away for a 117-107 win over the Houston Rockets

HOUSTON -- Ayo Dosunmu had 21 points and Jonathan Kuminga powered a fourth-quarter run that allowed the Minnesota Timberwolves to pull away for a 117-107 win over the Houston Rockets on Wednesday night.
Minnesota led by two before a 3-pointer from Kuminga, a steal by Dosunmu and a tip-in by Kuminga made it 111-104 with about two minutes remaining.
Kevin Durant made two free throws for Houston before another 3 by Kuminga extended the lead to 114-106 with less than a minute to go.
LaMelo Ball scored 12 of his 20 points in the fourth quarter for Minnesota after finishing with a season-high 34 in his previous game.

Alperen Sengun had his 13th career triple-double with 17 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists to lead the Rockets as they lost for just the second time this season. Durant added 21 points and Fred VanVleet had 18.
Kuminga finished with 16 points and eight rebounds. Jaden McDaniels had 14 points and eight boards for the Timberwolves.
The Rockets led by two midway through the fourth quarter before Ball scored seven points during a 10-2 run that gave the Timberwolves a 104-98 lead with about five minutes to play.
Sengun made one of two free throws before a 3-pointer by VanVleet got the Rockets within 104-102 about a minute later.

Already without star Anthony Edwards for up to two months after arthroscopic knee surgery, the Timberwolves also played without guard Terrence Shannon Jr., who missed his second straight game with a bruised hip.
Kuminga received a flagrant foul 1 in the second quarter after elbowing Sengun in the jaw and knocking him to the court.

title: LIV Golf is winding down operations, lawyer says in bankruptcy hearing
summary: LIV Golf is winding down its operations instead of launching a new version because of a lack of financial support
story: LIV Golf is winding down its operations instead of launching a new version because of a lack of financial support
TRENTON, N.J. -- TRENTON, N.J. (AP) — LIV Golf is winding down operations instead of launching a new version because of a lack of financial support.
A lawyer representing the organization announced the decision in a bankruptcy court hearing Thursday in New Jersey.
“The debtors are not currently proceeding with the LIV 2.0 plan,” Matthew Williams of Gibson Dunn said. “Instead, the debtors are toggling to a value-maximizing wind-down in their business."

LIV Golf lost Saudi Arabia funding in April after having spent more than $5 billion since 2022. LIV filed for bankruptcy in September. Since announcing plans for a new version, top players like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton have bailed.

The league was originally run by Greg Norman. A few months after the start of the Iran war, PIF changed its investment strategy in April and said it would no longer pay for LIV Golf after the 2026 season.
The Asian Tour, which received a financial boost from LIV for an International Series, decided in July to renew an alliance with the PGA Tour and European tour.

And as LIV was trying to emerge from bankruptcy, filed on Sept. 8, the European tour laid down a crushing ultimatum by saying anyone who signed with LIV 2.0 need not apply for membership in the commercially known DP World Tour.
That would make European players ineligible for the Ryder Cup.

Guy Kinnings, the European tour CEO, called out LIV in an interview with The Scotsman when he said, “But we also have to protect the tour against an entity who spent, so we are told, over $7 billion, with one of their aims being to ‘destroy the DP World Tour.’”

Rahm, Sergio Garcia, Louis Oosthuizen and Tyrrell Hatton also said they would no longer stay with LIV, and the rival league also lost young players like David Puig of Spain and Tom McKibbin of Northern Ireland.

The year began with Brooks Koepka getting out of his LIV deal with one year remaining, and the PGA Tour created a path — with financial penalties — to return. Patrick Reed chose not to extend his deal and now is poised to return to the PGA Tour next year through his performance in Europe.
Rahm had said on Tuesday he would be willing to pay the same price as Koepka, though it was unlikely that same deal would be offered.

LIV 2.0 was pushing player equity and prize money that was more than half the $20 million purses for individuals when it began in 2022. LIV’s final event was in August in Indianapolis, won by Michael La Sasso. He failed to get through the second stage of European tour Q-school last week.

title: Real Madrid hosts Falcons, home of world champion welcomes Bengals ahead of NFL game in Madrid
summary: The Atlanta Falcons have begun preparing for their NFL game in Madrid at the training center of Spanish soccer powerhouse Real Madrid
story: The Atlanta Falcons have begun preparing for their NFL game in Madrid at the training center of Spanish soccer powerhouse Real Madrid

MADRID -- The Atlanta Falcons began preparing for their NFL game in Madrid on Wednesday at the training center of Spanish soccer powerhouse Real Madrid, while the Cincinnati Bengals start practicing Thursday at the facilities of World Cup champion Spain.
Both teams departed to the capital on Tuesday for Sunday's game at Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu Stadium, home of the record 15-time European champion.

“This is a beautiful facility for us to get some work done this week,” Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said. “This is a huge undertaking to take your football team across the pond. And I’m just very appreciative and grateful to the NFL, to our organization. Amazing the amount of work that goes into this.
“I just get to show up and step on the plane and we’re here. But there’s so much work that goes into it, and I’m very appreciative to our group for taking great care of us.”
The Falcons went straight to Real Madrid’s training center for a workout.
It will be the second NFL regular-season game in Madrid after the Miami Dolphins beat the Washington Commanders 16-13 in overtime in last year's inaugural game in the country.

“There's always fine tuning that needs to be done, but everything seems to be going on track,” said Rafa de los Santos, the NFL country manager for Spain. “We’re super happy with the way that everything is going, at the stadium level, at the city level, at everything that has to do with the events that we have through the course of the week. Everything ready for a big Sunday.”

The game will include a moment to remember the victims of the high-speed train collision that killed 69 people and injured dozens last week. Organizers did not elaborate on the tribute, saying it will be a surprise.
The game in Madrid will be the seventh in a record nine-game schedule outside the U.S. for the NFL this season. The remaining games will be played in Munich and Mexico City.

Organizers expect “mint” field conditions at the Bernabeu, which is expected to welcome some 80,000 fans on Sunday. A crowd of 78,610 watched the game last year. Tickets were still available for this week’s game.

“The field at Bernabeu is always in good condition,” De los Santos said. “As you know, this is priority No. 1 for Real Madrid, and we’re super happy. We had a happy feeling about the field last year, and we don’t see any indication that this year is going to be any different. We are expecting to have the field in mint condition.”

Last year, the Commanders practiced at Real Madrid's training center and the Dolphins used the stadium facilities of city rival Atletico Madrid. This time, the Bengals chose the home of Spain, which played two matches at the Falcons' stadium in Atlanta during the World Cup earlier this year.

“The good thing is that this year the Falcons are having their practices at (Madrid's training center), and they’re super used to deal with high-level athletes as the Falcons are," De los Santos said. "And, of course, the (Spanish soccer) federation as well, they’re super used to having the world champions.”

The halftime show will feature Colombian music star Manuel Turizo, but organizers will again have to comply with local noise regulations at the Bernabeu, which is located in an upscale residential neighborhood.
Concerts at the stadium have been suspended since 2024 following complaints from neighbors about excessive noise.

“Everything that has to do with the halftime show, and the event itself, it will be under the law and the regulations that we have in Spain,” De los Santos said. “We adjust to the regulations. That’s what we do.”
Madrid and the NFL have another year left on their agreement for games in the Spanish capital.

title: Williamson's 23 points and Bey's clutch scoring lift the Pelicans past the Jazz, 120-113 in overtime
summary: Saddiq Bey closed out a 22-point performance with six straight points in the final minutes of overtime, and the New Orleans Pelicans rallied to defeat the Utah Jazz, 120-113
story: Saddiq Bey closed out a 22-point performance with six straight points in the final minutes of overtime, and the New Orleans Pelicans rallied to defeat the Utah Jazz, 120-113

NEW ORLEANS -- Saddiq Bey closed out a 22-point performance with six straight points in the final minutes of overtime, and the New Orleans Pelicans rallied to defeat the Utah Jazz 120-113 on Wednesday night.

Zion Williamson scored 23 points — all after halftime — as the Pelicans overcame a 13-point deficit late in the third quarter to pull out their fourth straight victory after four straight losses to open the season.

Dejounte Murray scored 20 points in his returned from a three-game absence after the birth of a child. Derik Queen scored 14 of his 20 points in the fourth quarter for the Pelicans, who played without Trey Murphy III (knee soreness).
Keyonte George scored 39 points and the Utah Jazz, who lost their sixth straight, and whose only victory this season came against New Orleans in Utah earlier this season.

George, who now has five 20-point games this season, hit consecutive 3s in the first minute of overtime to give Utah a 110-104 lead. But the Pelicans responded with 14 straight points, highlighted by Bey's off-balance, 6-footer that rolled all the way around the rim before falling in to make it 116-110 with 39 seconds left.
Lauri Markkanen had 21 points and 10 rebounds, hitting two 3s in the final 1:36 of regulation, the second giving Utah a 104-100 lead with 39 seconds left.

Williamson's driving layup and Murray's free throws tied it with 6.4 seconds left, and the game went to overtime — but only after George was a fraction of a second late getting off a pull-up jumper he hit over Williamson.
Official Courtney Kirkland left the court with with an apparent left leg injury during overtime, when the game was played with two officials.

Williamson, who also had two blocks and two steals. was held scoreless until he made two free throws with 8:49 remaining in the third quarter. He wound up with 13 points in the third period and his final four points came in overtime. Jeremiah Fears scored 19 points for New Orleans.

title: Bill Belichick again is among five coaching candidates for the Pro Football Hall of Fame
summary: Bill Belichick again is among five coaching candidates for the Pro Football Hall of Fame
story: Bill Belichick again is among five coaching candidates for the Pro Football Hall of Fame
Bill Belichick again is among five coaching candidates for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan join Belichick in the Coach category for possible election into the Hall’s Class of 2027.
The list was announced Thursday by the Canton, Ohio-based Pro Football Hall of Fame.

Members of the Hall’s coaching subcommittee made their selections from an original field of 14 nominees. The subcommittee will select one candidate to be considered when the Hall’s selection committee determines a new class of enshrinees in early 2027.

All five reached this stage last year when Belichick advanced in the process but the six-time Super Bowl champion head coach was not elected in his first year of eligibility. Belichick’s snub was criticized intensely around the NFL.

“If he’s not a first-ballot Hall of Famer, there’s really no coach that should ever be a first-ballot Hall of Famer, which is completely ridiculous because people deserve it. He’s incredible,” Tom Brady said.
Belichick and Brady won six Super Bowls with the New England Patriots. Belichick also won two as a defensive assistant coach with the New York Giants.

Belichick’s career included a sign-stealing scandal dubbed “Spygate” in the 2007 season. He was fined $500,000 after the team was caught filming defensive signals from the New York Jets during a game.
Belichick’s final season in New England was 2023. He’s in his second season coaching in college at North Carolina.

Coughlin won two Super Bowls with the Giants, beating Belichick, Brady and the Patriots both times. He was 182-157 in 20 seasons with the Giants and Jacksonville Jaguars. Coughlin also won a title with Giants as an assistant coach.

Holmgren led the Green Bay Packers to one Super Bowl title and was 174-122, including postseason, in 17 seasons with the Packers and Seattle Seahawks. He also won two Super Bowls as an assistant with the San Francisco 49ers.

Reeves was 201-174-2 in 23 seasons with the Denver Broncos, Giants and Atlanta Falcons. He led the Broncos to the Super Bowl three times and the Falcons once, going 0-4. Reeves won a title as an assistant with the Dallas Cowboys.
Shanahan won back-to-back Super Bowls with Denver and was 178-144 in 20 seasons with the Broncos and Washington Redskins. He also won a title with the 49ers as an assistant coach.
On Wednesday, the Hall of Fame announced the five contributors who have advanced in the process: Ralph Hay, Robert Kraft, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten.
The final list of 15 candidates will include one contributor, one coach and 13 modern-era players. The group will be reduced to 10 and then seven candidates.

A 25-person selection committee will be able to vote for six people, with 80% of support needed. The Hall said that would lead to a range of three to seven Hall of Famers each year, with by far the most likely number to get the necessary support being either five or six people.
The Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027 will be announced at “NFL Honors” in Los Angeles in February and enshrined next August in Canton.

Cooper made two 3s and Indrusaitis and Semetri Carr each hit one during a 12-2 surge that stretched the Golden Bears' lead to 71-58 with 7:16 remaining. Another 3 from Cooper with 4:32 to play gave Cal its largest lead, 79-62.
Radford had its last lead about three minutes into the first half and trailed 45-37 at the break. A 12-1 run in the second pulled the Highlanders to 52-51, but they couldn't take the lead.
Frederik Erichsen scored 16 points and grabbed eight rebounds for Radford (0-2). Ja’Corey Robinson had eight points to go with nine rebounds and five assists.
It was the first meeting between the teams.
Radford: On the road against No. 8 Tennessee on Monday.
Cal: Faces No. 10 Houston in the Lake Tahoe Classic on Sunday.

title: Valkyries' victory celebration includes Oakland where team practices, San Francisco where games are
summary: Gabby Williams hopped off a double-decker bus and began dancing through the streets, blowing a whistle to the beat and slapping high-fives with fans all while keeping her WNBA Finals MVP trophy safely tucked in her left arm
story: Gabby Williams hopped off a double-decker bus and began dancing through the streets, blowing a whistle to the beat and slapping high-fives with fans all while keeping her WNBA Finals MVP trophy safely tucked in her left arm

SAN FRANCISCO -- Gabby Williams hopped off a double-decker bus and began dancing through the streets, blowing a whistle to the beat and slapping high-fives with fans all while keeping her WNBA Finals MVP trophy safely tucked in her left arm.

Then she called for teammate Kiah Stokes to join her and they popped Champagne and enjoyed it among the first group in the Valkyries' victory parade on a picture-perfect Wednesday afternoon along San Francisco's waterfront.
“I love this,!” Stokes said, before joining in with the crowd chanting “MVP!” for Williams.

The Valkyries began their day of celebration at Oakland's Jack London Square neighborhood, not far from the team's downtown practice facility, then took a ferry across the bay to begin the parade from San Francisco's Ferry Building. It concluded near the San Francisco Giants' Oracle Park, and the baseball team's manager, Tony Vitello, was among those supporting the women's team on the route.
It was an important move for the team to honor and include both cities and the franchise's strong support systems from throughout Northern California.
Zaelani Fowler, 3, watched the parade with mom Brittanee and held a “Girl Power” sign with a heart saying “We Love” with each of the players' numbers.

“Making history,” the mother said. “To actually be here physically, it's amazing, and a beautiful thing that she's going to be able to look back at and say, ‘Wow, I was there when the Valkyries made history.' Girl power."

Fans were again encouraged by the team to “dare we say... call in sick?” when Golden State announced the afternoon parade along San Francisco's picturesque, popular bayfront after several thousand skipped out on work and school to attend a watch party on the big screen at Thrive City's plaza area outside Chase Center for Game 6 last Thursday, played at 9:30 a.m. Pacific time.

Avid Valkyries supporter Cynthia Cheak, who had her left leg amputated two years ago, was invited to be part of the parade. A former personal trainer who is always dressed in violet sparkles from head to toe, Cheak said handing out bracelets throughout “Ballhalla” gave her new purpose and improved her mental health. Cheak has gifted some 26,000 wristbands she purchased since July.

“It’s a humbling yet a powerful experience being able to ride in the Valkyries championship parade,” Cheak said. “Knowing that a simple wristband could bring so many people together, showing kindness, support, compassion and accessibility for all! Remembering that anything can happen if you don’t give up and believe in ‘Ballhalla’ and the Valkyries.”
The celebration came after the Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream 68-63 on Saturday night in the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. Williams scored 28 of her 30 points in the second half.

Three years ago when Golden State was granted an expansion franchise, owner Joe Lacob guaranteed a championship within five years — and this group led by coach Natalie Nakase delivered an improbable title in Year 2 after becoming the first expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in its inaugural year in 2025.
The Valkyries sensed how special this could be from the start and they played well together from Day 1.
“I believed it early, and we continued to get better,” point guard Veronica Burton said. “And I think that's when it was like, ‘OK, this is real, we’re going to do this,' and it happened.”

Williams heard from Michael Jordan among the many congratulations she received, and the star guard and her teammates also were honored on the court at Chase Center during the Golden State Warriors' game Sunday night.

On another double-decker bus, 14-year veteran Tiffany Hayes fittingly held the championship trophy, the 37-year-old guard having captured her first WNBA title at last after coming out of retirement two years ago to help the Valkyries win.

Kaitlyn Chen and Burton also climbed off a bus and made their way across The Embarcadero to greet fans, honoring those from “Ballhalla” who have meant so much to this bunch and the winning journey in just two years.
Later, the festivities continued as Williams and Stephen Curry held a fireside chat at a restaurant outside Chase Center. She has leaned on the 2022 NBA Finals MVP.

“Just having fun, enjoying the moment,” Williams said. “I was lucky enough to talk to this man next to me before Game 2 I think. He was like, ‘It’s a marathon, be ready for it, save your best for last, don't let your demeanor change.' That stuck with me. I had that playing in my head that second half.”
