title: Spencer Pratt says $1,200 hotel 'fortress' was cheaper than security as death threats mounted
summary: Spencer Pratt says death threats and armed security costs during the Los Angeles mayoral race made the Hotel Bel-Air the cheapest option available.
story: The 'Outnumbered' panel discusses Spencer Pratt’s claims that Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass mismanaged the Palisades wildfire response and the city’s homelessness crisis.
Spencer Pratt explained why his controversial stay at the Hotel Bel-Air was actually the cheaper option as he faced death threats while running for mayor of Los Angeles.

The 43-year-old reality star faced scrutiny in May after TMZ reported he had been staying at the luxury hotel despite appearing to suggest in a campaign ad that he was living in an Airstream trailer on the site of his California home, which was destroyed in the devastating Pacific Palisades fire.

At the time, the outlet reported that Pratt had been staying at the Hotel Bel-Air for more than a month, though "The Hills" alum disputed that characterization, saying he had spent no more than six days there during the previous month.
SPENCER PRATT’S MAYORAL RUN BACKED BY PARIS HILTON, KRISTIN CAVALLARI AS CELEBRITY DIVIDE DEEPENS
In a lengthy X post he shared Tuesday, Pratt, who lost in the June primary election, defended his choice to stay at the pricey hotel during the race.
"Why is he spending $1,200 a night? Why couldn’t he stay somewhere for $300 a night? Well, the answer to that question is not as pretty as any of us may like to hear," Pratt wrote.
Spencer Pratt defended his controversial $1,200 a night hotel stay as the cheapest option. (Getty Images)
REALITY TV STAR SPENCER PRATT GAINS TRACTION IN LOS ANGELES MAYORAL RACE AFTER FIERY DEBATE

"Most people simply presumed that I was being a bougie spoiled brat, and that I was abusing campaign funds," he continued. "They expected me to stay at a cheaper hotel, but what they don’t realize is … the Hotel Bel Air was the cheapest hotel in all of LA.

"At the time, I couldn’t explain the math to people, and my campaign staff told me I wasn’t allowed to divulge the real reason I had to stay there, but now that the election is coming to a close, I don’t need to listen to anyone anymore."
'ENTOURAGE' CREATOR BACKS SPENCER PRATT FOR LA MAYOR, SAYS CITY 'HAS COLLAPSED' UNDER CURRENT LEADERSHIP

Pratt had previously told TMZ in May that the Airstream had become unsafe, saying that the Bel Air Hotel's "armed security" made it "the only option." He claimed that supporters of his opponents, Mayor Karen Bass and City Councilmember Nithya Raman were "getting increasingly desperate and hostile" due to his performance at the May debate and strong polling numbers.
Pratt said the hotel "fortress" was less costly than round-the-clock security. (Highfive/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)
"I can't talk about specific threats, but that lot is ... unsafe now," he said at the time.
JIMMY KIMMEL ATTACKS FIRE VICTIM SPENCER PRATT AS 'SCREAMING JERK,' LECTURES LA VOTERS ABOUT MAYORAL ELECTION
In his X post, Pratt, who ran as a Republican, elaborated on the threats that he received, which he attributed to political violence.

"Throughout the campaign, I endured numerous death threats, to the point where I had to hire full-time security," he wrote. "Anyone who’s had to hire security knows that they will always tell you to not discuss your death threats; they find that it often has the opposite effect you would expect; normal people should hear it and think ‘whoa, we need to dial back the temperature, this isn’t acceptable’, but the reality is that commie street animals get inspired, and you will end up getting copycats if you advertise your threats."
SPENCER PRATT VOWS TO LEAVE LA AND FIND 'LAST AMERICAN DREAM' IN ANOTHER CITY IF MAYORAL BID FAILS
Pratt went on to detail specific incidents he said led him to fear for his safety and that of his family.
"People were breaking into my lot in the Palisades and leaving notes on the airstream with white powder in them," he wrote.
DEM MAYOR FACES REALITY CHECK AFTER ACCUSING RIVAL OF 'EXPLOITING' PALISADES FIRE: 'ABSOLUTE TONE DEAFNESS'

The TV personality also claimed that a "lunatic" who was "hellbent on tracking me down" charged at his young son while he was boogie-boarding in the ocean. Pratt shares sons Gunner, 8, and Ryker, 3, with his wife and former "The Hills" co-star Heidi Montag, 40.

"So, I had to hire a second security detail for my family while I was away campaigning," he wrote. "I don’t know if you’ve ever had to hire 4-5 armed security professionals with blacked out SUVs, but…it’s not cheap. One of the first things they told me was that my lot in the Palisades was a security nightmare; perched mid-slope on a hill, totally exposed in a bowl, surrounded by elevated positions where a shooter could easily traipse through the wilderness of the State Park, and have a clear line of sight to every inch of my property.
SPENCER PRATT: LOS ANGELES ANGRY WITH KAREN BASS’ MISMANAGEMENT
"I wasn’t allowed to stay on that property, even if I wanted to," he added. "Enter the Hotel Bel Air."
Pratt explained that the famed LA hotel, which has hosted celebrities, presidents and royalty, is an unusually secure property due to its design.
"The Hills" alum faced backlash when it was revealed he was not living in the Airstream trailer on his Pacific Palisades lot.  (HighFive/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)
PRATT CONCEDES LA MAYOR RACE WITH SCATHING VIDEO TEASING NEXT MOVE, BOMBSHELL INFO HE HOLDS: 'COMMIE ANIMALS'
"While $1,200 a night isn’t very unique for a decent hotel in a major city, there’s something else about the hotel that is unique," Pratt wrote.

"Unlike my turkey shoot of a lot in the Palisades, the Hotel Bel Air is surrounded with a fortress wall, with a single point of ingress, a fatal funnel that takes you over a moat, just to enter the property. You then must navigate a labyrinth of walled off bungalows, and it is very easy to get lost. Unlike normal hotels, it is a very secure facility.
"When my security team dropped me off behind the walls of the Bel Air, they felt good about leaving me alone in the secure facility," he continued.

"Had I stayed anywhere else, I would have needed to book out 3 rooms for my team to maintain overnight security, which would’ve cost an additional $3,000 per night. Paradoxically, by this calculation, I was actually saving a ton of money by staying at the secure Bel Air; even staying at a Motel 6 would’ve cost me more money, and in a campaign…money is everything."

Pratt argued that Republicans face a "permanent fundraising disadvantage" due to safety expenses.  (Robert Gauthier/Los Angeles Times)

title: Bruce Springsteen sparks fan fury after backing Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
summary: Bruce Springsteen's endorsement of Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate race drew fierce backlash from fans citing antisemitism concerns.
story: Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo discusses the star's 'sermon' about the United States on 'The Ingraham Angle.'
Bruce Springsteen has a message for Michigan voters — and some of his longtime fans aren't having it.
The rock legend faced criticism from some social media users after backing Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, prompting angry fans to accuse The Boss of crossing a political line.
2026 MIDTERM ELECTION DAY RESULTS: LIVE UPDATES
Springsteen, who has never shied away from politics, took aim at President Donald Trump in his endorsement of El-Sayed, portraying the progressive candidate as a defender of American democracy.

"Dr. El-Sayed is a fighter for our American Constitution, he’s a fighter for our American Democracy, and he’s a fighter against the corrupt, lawless, and anti-American leadership currently in the White House. That’s why I’m in his corner 100%. Bruce Springsteen," he penned on social media.
CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT

Bruce Springsteen faced criticism from fans after endorsing Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, with some calling the rock legend's political support "unforgivable." (Gareth Cattermole / Getty Images For BFI; Chip Somodevilla / Getty Images)
Critics questioned why the New Jersey-born singer was endorsing El-Sayed, given controversies over the candidate's political associations and positions on Israel.

"Bruce Springsteen, the guy who spent 40 years cashing in on ‘Born in the USA,’ finally posts after two years of silence just to call an elected American president ‘corrupt, lawless, and anti-American’ while locking arms with Abdul El-Sayed, the same guy who campaigned with Hasan Piker (the streamer who said America deserved 9/11) and still can’t shake the Muslim Brotherhood questions about his own family."

Bruce Springsteen expresses support for Dr. El-Sayed in a statement shared on social media, calling him a fighter for the American Constitution and democracy and criticizing the current White House leadership. (Bruce Springsteen / Instagram)
METALLICA FRONTMAN JAMES HETFIELD BLASTS ENTERTAINERS PUSHING POLITICAL AGENDAS AT CONCERTS

Another commenter criticized the singer's political activism, writing, "The Boss isn’t fighting for the Constitution. He’s just another rich coastal has-been who needs a new reason to hate the country that made him."

"Bruce Springsteen who performed at the concert for NY at MSG on 2001 after 9/11….. is now campaigning for a Muslim brotherhood sympathizer," another person wrote. "Did I not have this on my bingo card for today."
Bruce Springsteen has a long history of criticizing President Donald Trump. (Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic; Chen Mengtong/China News Service/VCG via Getty Images)
Another longtime fan expressed sadness and anger over what they viewed as Springsteen's failure to understand the impact of his endorsement on those who have long fought antisemitism.

"Shame on you. You are not educated to understand what your endorsement means to so many life long fans and good people that are fighting antisemitism and hatred for thousands of years. You are acting like an ignorant uneducated school child. You did this for what reason? This is so foolish. I’m so sad., I’m 59 years old.. Shame on me for thinking you were educated and smarter. Take the time to understand the other point of view."
However, not everyone was ready to turn on the rock icon.
EL-SAYED'S SILENCE OVER MOM'S FBI QUESTIONING RAISES TRANSPARENCY CONCERNS
Some Bruce Springsteen fans accused The Boss of crossing a political line. (Talia Sprague/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Springsteen's endorsement drew support from El-Sayed backers, including one self-described frequent concertgoer who accused critics of unfairly targeting the Democratic candidate.

"As a huge Springsteen fan, and veteran of over 50 different shows around the country, and a resident of Michigan, and supporter of Dr. Abdul El Sayed, I support this message 100%. I suspect that some of your Jewish fans may have issues with this, but that's their problem. That just shows their bigotry. They're the first ones to … complain about the racism and bigotry of Maga, and yet here they are doing the same damn thing to Abdul. Anyway Bruce, thank you for supporting the good Dr. and always being on the side of the good guys."
"Fully with you, he's the man," one supporter wrote.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
"Thank you Bruce. History is about to be made. Abdul is more than qualified," another added.
Another commenter questioned El-Sayed's political beliefs and policy positions.

"Would love to know exactly what El-Sayed’s beliefs and what he is doing that American you love so much? America is not a socialist country nor is socialism the USA’s belief no matter who has been in the Oval Office."
Democratic Senate Candidate Abdul El-Sayed speaks during a campaign town hall at Cadillac High School on October 10, 2026, in Cadillac, Michigan. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, El-Sayed's Republican opponent, former Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich., accused the Democratic candidate of misleading Michigan voters about his views on the Muslim Brotherhood, pointing to reported associations involving members of El-Sayed's family.

El-Sayed previously told Fox News that he has "never been" and will "never be" a member of the Muslim Brotherhood. Fox News Digital is not aware of any direct ties between El-Sayed and the organization.
Springsteen also released a second video message addressing election officials and government representatives, urging them to protect the integrity of the voting process.
"Hi, it’s Bruce Springsteen. I’m speaking to election officials and representatives of our government on election day. You have sworn an oath to preserve, protect, and defend our constitution."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

He continued, "That means you have a solemn duty to ensure that our votes are securely counted. Thomas Jefferson said, government requires the consent of the governed. You who represent us must never consent to any directives that undermine our constitutional right to a free and fair election. Our vote is our voice, and it’s up to you to ensure that our voice is heard. I wish you all a good election day, and thank you for your service."

Bruce Springsteen's endorsement of Abdul El-Sayed drew increased attention to Michigan's Senate race, where the Democrat is facing Republican Mike Rogers. (Sarah Rice/Getty Images; Alex Wong/Getty Images)
The accompanying caption urged followers who had not yet voted to do so and directed them to OathProject.org to take what Springsteen described as an "Oath to the Constitution."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

The endorsement comes as El-Sayed faces Rogers in a Michigan U.S. Senate race. El-Sayed, a former Wayne County health official, is running on a progressive platform centered on universal healthcare after defeating Rep. Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary.

The race has featured disagreements over U.S. support for Israel and accusations of antisemitism. Stevens endorsed Rogers, who is seeking a political comeback after losing the 2024 Senate race by fewer than 20,000 votes.
Fox News Digital has reached out to Springsteen and El-Sayed for comment.

title: John Rich says Kathy Hochul is ‘running over’ NY farmers with renewable energy agenda
summary: John Rich's country song "Dear Kathy" takes aim at Governor Kathy Hochul over renewable energy policies he says are silencing upstate New York farmers.
story: Country singer John Rich accused the New York governor of helping redefine prime farmland and creating a "chokeout" for farmers through ORES.
John Rich is blasting New York Gov. Kathy Hochul over the state’s renewable energy policies, accusing her administration of silencing farmers and overriding local officials in upstate New York.

The 52-year-old Big & Rich member has publicly joined local landowners, activists and officials who are challenging New York’s Office of Renewable Energy Siting (ORES), a state agency that reviews and permits major renewable energy and transmission projects.

Last month, Rich released his new country song "Dear Kathy," which is directed at the Democratic governor, who is running for re-election. In the song, Rich speaks on behalf of farmers and landowners who are protesting large-scale solar and wind projects on upstate New York farmland, arguing that ORES has undermined local control and put family farms, rural communities and private property rights at risk.
JOHN RICH WARNS NASHVILLE'S FAMED BROADWAY COULD GO DARK AS BUSINESSES FACE TAX ‘DEATH NAIL’
During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, Rich shared his message for Hochul, pointing to the final line of "Dear Kathy," which asks, "Why do you hate these people so much?"
"What have they ever done to you except pay taxes and put food on your table? That’s it," Rich said.
"Why do you hate these people?" he continued. "Because only somebody that has a vindictive spirit would do what she’s doing to them — or greed."
John Rich slammed New York Gov. Kathy Hochul over the state's renewable energy policies. (Jason Kempin/Getty Images; James Carbone/Newsday RM via Getty Images)

"I think greed is probably the largest driver in it because these companies that are coming in, building these huge fields. Listen, if you add up all the plans they have coming into upstate New York, it’s over 100 square miles of solar panels," Rich added.
WILLIE NELSON URGES AMERICANS TO FIGHT 'WATER THIEVING' AI DATA CENTERS DEVOURING RURAL TEXAS FARMLAND

The conflict centers on New York’s centralized permitting system for large-scale solar and wind projects. Created in 2020 under former Gov. Andrew Cuomo, ORES generally handles renewable energy projects capable of producing 25 megawatts or more. Its rules encourage developers to avoid the state’s most productive agricultural soils and require them to minimize or mitigate impacts when farmland cannot be avoided.

ORES can also waive local zoning and land-use restrictions it deems "unreasonably burdensome," a power that critics argue gives state officials too much control over farmland and leaves local communities with limited say over projects in their areas.
BROOKE ROLLINS, MONICA CROWLEY: AMERICA’S FAMILY FARMS HAVE KEPT US STRONG FOR 250 YEARS

While speaking with Fox News Digital, Rich claimed Hochul’s administration used research from Cornell University to change how prime farmland is defined. The singer argued that the move made it easier for solar and wind projects to be built on agricultural land.
WATCH: JOHN RICH SLAMS KATHY HOCHUL OVER FARMLAND DISPUTE: ‘WHY DO YOU HATE THESE PEOPLE?’

"She decided she didn’t like their definition of prime farmland because if it’s prime, it’s protected from solar and wind and projects like that," Rich said. "So they just redefined it. They just came up with a whole new equation and determined, well, based on these new numbers, there’s really no such thing as prime farmland anymore in upstate New York. So we can do whatever the hell we want to these people."
AMISH FACE NEW YORK VACCINE MANDATE IN SUPREME COURT FIGHT, MIGHT HAVE TO ‘PACK THEIR WAGONS’

"Oh, by the way, we put ORES in place. So if they try to stop us, we just run right over the top of them," he continued. "I mean, it is a complete and total chokeout that she’s put on these farmers up there."

"Some of these families have owned their farms, been in their families since before the Revolutionary War," Rich said. "You’re talking about one of the original 13 colonies, New York, and to think that 250 years later, after these same people’s ancestors had to fight off the British, now they’re standing there fighting with their own governor in the United States of America."
"It is astonishing, and I find it to be disgusting. I also think it’s probably unconstitutional," he added.
Rich said that the policies are silencing upstate New York farmers. (Getty Images)

Since taking office in 2021, Hochul has continued to advance New York’s renewable energy agenda. Her administration has promoted large-scale solar and wind development and defended the state’s approach to farmland, arguing that renewable energy projects are not taking over New York’s "best farmland" and that leasing land for solar can help farmers keep their property in their families.
When reached for comment by Fox News Digital, Hochul’s office pushed back on Rich’s criticism.

"If he really wants to help farmers, maybe he can write a song calling on his buddy Donald Trump to lift the tariffs, end his reckless war with Iran that is driving up gas and diesel prices, and rein in the ICE raids, all of which are hurting farmers here in New York and across the country," Ken Lovett, a senior communications adviser on energy and environment for Hochul, said.
DEBRA MESSING DITCHES DEMOCRAT FOR TRUMP-BACKED REPUBLICAN AS SHE SOUNDS ALARM OVER NEW YORK

Rich said he first learned about the dispute after seeing Alexandra Fasulo, an upstate New York landowner and ORES critic, discuss it on social media. The singer said he was startled by the claim that the state could sideline landowners, zoning boards, mayors and other local officials when deciding where major projects would be built.
"I said, that can’t be the case. I’m gonna go up and see this for myself," Rich recalled.
Rich argued that ORES' authority undermines "home rule," the principle that landowners and local governments should have authority over how land in their communities is used.
During his visit, Rich held two town hall meetings, including one at Fasulo’s farm, where he met with hundreds of farmers and landowners.
"We had Amish people standing in the room being silent, standing in the back," Rich said. "It looked like something out of a movie."

"And we had this discussion about ‘What are we going to do about this governor running over everybody?’" he continued. "And man, the sentiment in the room was so much frustration and feeling of bewilderment that what do you do? I mean, she's put something into gear here that just runs us over and takes away our voice."
The singer said that meeting with farmers inspired his protest song "Dear Kathy." (Anna Connors - Pool/Getty Images)
The singer told Fox News Digital that the meetings ultimately inspired him to write "Dear Kathy."

"I left there thinking to myself, I need to put this song out, ‘Dear Kathy,’" he recalled. "I need to write a song for the governor of New York on behalf of all those people whose voices she has silenced. And so that led to me with a pencil and a piece of paper and a guitar writing a letter or a song to Kathy Hochul."
WATCH: JOHN RICH SAYS MEETING AMISH FARMERS INSPIRED SONG TARGETING KATHY HOCHUL

On Oct. 28, Rich officially released the song and its accompanying music video, which highlights affected areas in upstate New York, showcasing local landowners and the Holy Trinity Monastery in Jordanville, NY, which has actively opposed large wind projects near its grounds.

"And I jokingly say in the video, 'What do you get the woman who has everything, including your freedom in her back pocket? Well, you give her the one thing she doesn't have — a country song,'" Rich said. "And so I wrote ‘Dear Kathy’ and it really was my way of speaking on behalf of those people that she will not listen to."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Rich described "Dear Kathy" as a "fight song" for the farmers he met and emphasized that the dispute transcended party lines.

WATCH: JOHN RICH CALLS ‘DEAR KATHY’ A ‘FIGHT SONG’ FOR NEW YORK FARMERS

"One interesting thing about those farmers that I met — they were Democrat, Republican, probably more Democrat than Republican, actually," he said. "And so it's not a partisan thing. Owning land is an American thing. I mean it may be one of the last things we all agree on in this country is that if you own land, if you bought that land, and you take care of that land, that's your land."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"You get to determine what happens to it or what doesn't happen to it," he continued. "And that's exactly what I felt up there. It was an across the board repudiation of Kathy Hochul and her assault on their land and on them and on their legacies."
Rich described "Dear Kathy" as a "fight song" for the farmers and landowners. (Tim Mosenfelder/WireImage/Getty Images)

"To me, as bad as that is, that was a beautiful experience actually for me to sit up there knowing that this is not a partisan deal, and I'm sitting in the room with both sides of the aisle, but everybody is in unison," Rich added.
Despite his criticism of Hochul, Rich told Fox News Digital that he would welcome the opportunity to meet with Hochul to discuss the landowners’ concerns directly.

"If Kathy Hochul wanted to sit with me and have a meeting, I would jump on the next thing smoking to be up there," he said. "I mean, I would sit down at her desk. She could bring anybody she wants and I would just ask questions. ‘Why do you think this is OK? I mean you're still an American. Don't you think that this is against the Constitution? Home rule is a real thing. You don't think that people that you govern have the right to determine what happens to their own land and not just a farm here or there, a hundred square miles of land?' I would just ask her basic questions."

title: 'Homestead' star Bailey Chase says California vaccine plans were 'final straw' that drove family out of LA
summary: Bailey Chase reveals the proposed COVID-19 vaccine mandate that drove his family from California to the mountains of North Carolina five years ago.
story: "Homestead" star  Bailey Chase tells Fox News Digital his family is now "living our best life" in North Carolina after leaving Los Angeles five years ago.
"Homestead" star Bailey Chase is opening up about the "final straw" that drove him and his family out of California for a new life in North Carolina.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 54-year-old actor, who shares daughter Waverly, 12, and 10-year-old twins Maggie and Gauge with his wife Amy, explained that concerns over how California's COVID-19 restrictions would impact his children led him to leave the Golden State behind.
"That happened five years ago in the throes of COVID," Chase said. "My wife and I picked up sticks with our three young children when they were mandating vaccines out there."

"They said they couldn't go back to school without it," Chase, who stars as former Green Beret Jeff Eriksson in "Homestead," continued. "And that was the final straw. And we've been in the mountains of North Carolina ever since living our best life."
Bailey Chase revealed that California's COVID-19 vaccine mandates for schools was the "final straw" that led him and his family to pack up and leave Los Angeles. (FilmMagic)
ZACHARY LEVI SAYS TEXAS GIVES HIM THE ‘FREEDOM’ HE COULDN’T FIND IN CALIFORNIA
Five years after trading Los Angeles for North Carolina, Chase told Fox News Digital that his life now largely revolves around his children's activities when he isn't working.
'VIRGIN RIVER' STAR BEN HOLLINGSWORTH SAYS HIS KIDS HAVE FREEDOM IN SMALL TOWN THAT 'DOESN'T FLY' IN LA

"I'm like soccer dad right now. It's soccer season, so we're going here and there," he said. "My oldest is really into ballet, and I couldn't be more proud of her and getting ready for ‘The Nutcracker’ in December, and basketball season's around the corner."
While Chase remains committed to his acting career, the "Longmire" alum said his priorities shift completely when he returns home.
CHRIS PRATT SAYS HIS FAITH WILL BE 'THE MOST IMPORTANT THING' THAT HE PASSES ON TO HIS KIDS
"I love my job, and when I'm off filming, I'm 100% focused on that. But when I'm home, I'm home," he said. "There's no greater job than being a dad."

Chase and his family currently live in Amy's hometown of Hendersonville in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Western North Carolina, about 25 miles south of Asheville. Chase has previously explained that Amy had long envisioned eventually returning to the area where she was born and raised. The actor also has ties to North Carolina after attending Duke University in Durham on a football scholarship.
'RANSOM CANYON' STAR JOSH DUHAMEL SAYS HE'D RATHER PUT MONEY INTO NORTH DAKOTA AFTER SELLING LOS ANGELES HOME

"Amy, being from the mountains of North Carolina, always had it in the back of her mind that she’d go back home one day," he said in a January 2026 interview with Duke Alumni Magazine. "We didn’t know how or when."
However, Chase recalled they decided the time was right due to California's handling of the pandemic.
Chase and his family moved to his wife Amy's hometown in North Carolina. (Getty Images)
‘TWILIGHT’ STAR KELLAN LUTZ TRADED CALIFORNIA FOR TENNESSEE LAND AND BIBLE STUDIES

"Things started to not work in LA during COVID – they shut down the schools, there were no sports for the kids," he said. "Really, no life, no work. And it became more and more obvious that we should leave LA."

"Amy’s very close with her parents, who are in N.C.," he continued. "Everything’s about seven minutes away: school, the in-laws, the grocery store, golf course, soccer field. It’s a great location. We live in a house that would not have been affordable in LA."
JANA KRAMER SAYS LOS ANGELES PRICED HER OUT OF THE CHILDHOOD SHE WANTED FOR HER KIDS
"It’s a kid’s dream," he added. "There’s a sports court and a pool. We have two golden retriever puppies, so it’s a full and lively house."

During a February appearance on the "Undaunted.Life: A Man's Podcast," Chase elaborated on the concerns that he had over California's proposed vaccine mandate for his young children's return to school.
"At that time, you know, they're 4, 4 and 6 years old," he recalled. "I got two young girls and, you know we don't need to go down that rabbit hole."
"I was like, 'No, I just don't know enough,'" he continued. "And I got one job right now, and it's to take care of these little nuggets. That's the most important job I have right now."

In October 2021, California Gov. Gavin Newsom announced plans for a COVID-19 vaccine requirement for students that he said would eventually apply to all the state's 6.7 million public and private schoolchildren.

However, the mandate was repeatedly delayed and ultimately never took effect. In February 2023, state health officials announced that they would not pursue or implement the requirement as the COVID-19 state of emergency expired at the end of that month.
The "Homestead" star said they are "living our best life." (Getty Images)
'ANT-MAN' STAR EVANGELINE LILLY SAYS SHE LEFT HOLLYWOOD BECAUSE SHE 'ALWAYS HATED BEING FAMOUS'

Chase previously acknowledged that while relocating to North Carolina was the best move for his family, leaving LA came at a professional cost after he spent 21 years building his career in Hollywood.
"I've lost out on some work by not being in L.A.," he admitted while appearing on the "Living Local" podcast in August.
"There was a big role on 'Grey's Anatomy,'" he continued. "And I understand, it's a lot cheaper for them. They just move on to the next guy and cast someone who's local to L.A."
"But what has happened is I've gotten new opportunities and different kind of jobs and some faith-based films and shows," Chase added.
The "Saving Grace" actor has also spoken openly about how he "lost touch" with God during his years in LA and shared that moving to North Carolina eventually led him back to his Christian faith.

"Moving back here, I've gotten reconnected to my faith," Chase told "Crosswalk" in January. "Just started going to church recently. It took a few years, but I really like the church where we're going to here."
"My cousin started taking us," he continued. "The girls are in youth group. They really love it."
"It's nice to be in an environment where I can openly talk about God and Jesus and without fear of criticism," he added.
WATCH HERE: ‘HOMESTEAD’ STAR BAILEY CHASE SAYS CALIFORNIA VACCINE PLANS WERE ‘FINAL STRAW’ THAT DROVE FAMILY OUT OF LA
In a 2024 Instagram post, Chase reflected on how his priorities have shifted since leaving behind "all that worry, all that stress, 20 years of hustle in LA."
"It also got me thinking if I spent as much time chasing God as I’ve spent chasing success the last 25 years, what would that look like?" he wrote.

Jesse Hutch, Kearran Giovanni, Georgie White, Emmanuel McCord, Colby Strong, Bailey Chase, Neal McDonough, Dawn Olivieri, Olivia Sanabia, Tyler Lofton and Kevin Lawson attend the "Homestead" premiere on Dec. 10, 2024. in LA. (Tommaso Boddi/Getty Images for Angel Studios)

Chase is currently starring as former Green Beret Jeff Eriksson in the faith-based streaming platform Angel Studios’ post-apocalyptic drama "Homestead," which will premiere its second season on Nov. 3.

The series follows survivors living at a fortified prepper compound in the Rocky Mountains known as The Homestead after a nuclear attack on LA plunges the country into chaos. After the bomb is detonated, Jeff escapes with his family to The Homestead, where he serves as head of security.

The actor starred in the 2024 theatrical movie "Homestead," which introduces the story and the TV series picks up directly afterward. The cast also includes Neal McDonough, Kevin Lawson Emmanuel McCord, Jesse Hutch, Betzaida Landín, Charles Esten and Dawn Olivieri.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Chase told Fox News Digital that starring in the "Homestead" movie and follow-up TV show had inspired the cast to start prepping for a potential apocalypse.
Chase is currently starring as former Green Beret Jeff Eriksson in the show. (Angel Studios)

"'Homestead' has changed all of our lives and the first thing I did when I came home after the film was arm my home more," he said. "And then right before season two, Hurricane Helene hit here in the mountains of North Carolina. And I now have a brand-new generator and some other things."
When asked if most Americans would be able to survive a major disaster, Chase predicted that it would be more challenging for people who live in bigger cities.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
"They're overpopulated and there aren't enough resources," he said. "So for those who are a little bit more in the country, their odds are a lot higher."
Chase also starred in the 2024 "Homestead" movie. (Angel Studios )
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
"Those are the kind of people who hunt and fish and can go out and find their own game," Chase added. "So if I'm laying odds, I'm betting on those guys."

While reflecting on what drew him to "Homestead," Chase explained that his focus on faith and family has also influenced the projects he chooses, noting that the show offers a different message than much of what is coming out of Hollywood.
"I take my job as being a father as the best job and most important job that I'll ever have. And I do take it seriously," Chase told Fox News Digital.

"And how that translates to me being an actor, that's why I'm so proud of ‘Homestead’ and the story that we get to tell, because it reflects my own personal values," he continued. "We got men and women and boys and girls, and it's about promoting faith, family, community and being there for your brother."
"Not all the shows that Hollywood's putting out does that, so I feel truly blessed to be part of a show that delivers a message that I believe in so deeply to my core."
"Homestead: The Series" season two premieres Nov. 3 on Angel with new episodes released weekly on Tuesdays.

title: 'DWTS' judge Carrie Ann Inaba speaks out on lift controversy after Val Chmerkovskiy suspension
summary: Carrie Ann Inaba revealed she and Jenna Johnson "hugged it out" after the lift rule controversy and Val Chmerkovskiy's suspension from "DWTS."
story: The "Boy Meets World" alum says partner Pasha Pashkov has helped her embrace confidence on and off the dance floor.
Carrie Ann Inaba addressed recent controversies on "Dancing With the Stars" with one swift social media post.

Inaba embraced Jenna Johnson in one image captured during the Oct. 20 show, the same episode where Johnson's husband, Val Chmerkovskiy, was suspended after sharing an inappropriate image online aimed at the judge.
During last month's episode, Inaba criticized Johnson's lifts, to which the dancer received a reading after she pushed back.
VAL CHMERKOVSKIY SUSPENDED FROM 'DANCING WITH THE STARS' OVER WILL SMITH OSCARS SLAP REFERENCE
Carrie Ann Inaba talked about how negative comments hurt her mental health. (Getty Images)

"I have not spoken about what happened because of professional courtesy for those who are still competing, and we actually have standards and practices that keep us separated," Inaba wrote on Instagram.

"I think it’s important for everyone to know that Jenna and I hugged it out after the Super Bowl show. Jenna was an absolute professional about it, and two women worked through the moment. It came to my attention later that Jenna was deeply hurt. So I also offered to speak with her at anytime."
JOHN STAMOS TOLD 'DANCING WITH THE STARS' PRODUCERS TO NEVER ASK HIM TO JOIN THE SHOW AGAIN

She added, "I have also offered to discuss the lift rule and how I enforce it. @ sharnaburgess made a great video explaining lifts, assists and which dances allow and don’t allow them. I think in the future, a new lift rule should be created for next season."
Inaba received criticism in the past for docking points over lifts, with fans claiming she picks and chooses when to apply her rule.

"I think in the future, a new lift rule should be created for next season," she commented. "I think a session of with all the dancers and the judges in a room together to discuss the history of how and why Len Goodman, our original producers and I defined the lift rule and the what the purpose is which is safety and fairness. [sic]"
CARRIE ANN INABA SHARES HER STRUGGLE TO MANAGE HIDDEN, INVISIBLE ILLNESS: 'IT'S REAL'
"The show has evolved tremendously, the way the show is cast has also changed, and so has our audience and the way they consume the show."
"DWTS" judge Carrie Ann Inaba admitted to being harder on the female contestants. (Getty Images)
Inaba added, "So, working together to create a better understanding between the dancers and the judges and our audience is important to me, as we move forward and is something I have asked for."
Chmerkovskiy was suspended from "DWTS" after appearing to reference Will Smith’s infamous Oscars slap in a since-deleted social media post defending Johnson.

"The well-being of everyone who works on ‘Dancing with the Stars’ is non-negotiable," BBC Studios said in a statement. "Val’s social media post was inappropriate and does not reflect the values or standards expected of anyone connected with the show. As a result, he will not participate in next week’s show."
Carrie Ann Inaba is the only female judge on "Dancing with the Stars." (Getty Images)

title: Chris Pratt went from living in a van to Hollywood stardom after chance encounter changed everything
summary: Chris Pratt recalls the moment Rae Dawn Chong walked into Bubba Gump Shrimp Company and offered him a role that launched his Hollywood career.
story: The actor opened up to Fox News Digital about fatherhood and admitted he hopes to learn from both his own father’s strengths and mistakes while raising his children.
Chris Pratt's journey to becoming one of Hollywood's go-to action stars started with him living in a van in Hawaii.

In a recent post on X, the 47-year-old actor reflected on his beginnings: "Before Hollywood, I was living in a van in Hawaii and waiting tables at Bubba Gump Shrimp Company," revealing that a chance encounter working one night changed his life.

"One day, the incredible Rae Dawn Chong walked into the restaurant, and naturally, I went up to her table and said, 'Hey, you’re a movie star! What are you doing here?'" he recalled. "She asked if I could act, and I said, 'F- - - yeah, put me in your movie!'"
Since he didn't have a phone, he gave Chong his friend Mike's number, who told him a few days later that someone had called for him.
Pratt reflected on the early days of his career in a recent social media post. (Mike Coppola/Getty Images)
NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER

"I called her back, and sure enough, she was serious," he wrote. "I drove over to pick up the script, went back to Mike’s house, and read all 120 pages three times in a row. First script I’d ever read. My character's name was Devon, and I remember thinking, 'Sweet! I could totally play a Devon!'
After the audition, he recalled Chung telling him he "could act and offered me the part."

While he lived in Hawaii, the movie was filming in Los Angeles, which made Pratt a little nervous, as he had "about $60 to my name, a bag of clothes, and some rollerblades." He then found out that Chung would fly him out to Los Angeles for production.

"I remember thinking right then and there, my life just changed forever. I'm going to be an actor," he wrote. "That little movie was 'Cursed Part 3,' a low-budget horror comedy that opened the door to Hollywood for me. I'll forever be grateful to Rae for taking a chance on a kid working at a shrimp restaurant. Everybody starts somewhere, and this is where it all began for me."

Pratt had $60 to his name when he was offered a part in his first movie. (Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images)
Pratt's role in "Cursed Part 3" led to bigger projects, including his breakout role playing Andy Dwyer in the hit NBC show, "Parks and Recreation."

He then landed the role of Peter Quill, or Star-Lord, in the Marvel movie, "Guardians of the Galaxy," playing the character in the film's two sequels, as well as in "Avengers: Infinity War" and "Avengers: Endgame."
Pratt credited James Gunn for changing his life. (Charley Gallay/Getty Images for Disney)

When speaking to Moviefone in May 2023, Pratt shared he is "grateful" for "Guardians of the Galaxy" director James Gunn for casting him as the lead in the movie, saying, "He's changed my life" and the life of his children.

"He found a working actor who had already at that point done way better than most people who come out to town. I wasn't a waiter any longer, I was a series regular on a show. I was getting recognition," he said. "He brought me to a whole new level that ultimately changed the entire way the industry saw me. I no longer was auditioning. That was the last audition I ever had. So he changed my life."

Pratt went on to star in a number of successful projects. (Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images)

Since becoming a Marvel superhero, Pratt has starred in the "Jurassic World" franchise, voiced characters in "The Lego Movie" and its sequel, "The Super Mario Bros. Movie" and its sequel and "Onward," and has starred in the TV series "The Terminal List" since 2022.
He has also starred in a number of standalone blockbusters, including "Passengers," "The Magnificent Seven," "The Tomorrow War" and many others.

Chris Pratt stars in "The Terminal List." (Marni Grossman/Prime)
Pratt was married to actress Anna Faris from July 2009 to August 2017, when they announced their separation. They share one child together, a son named Jack, 14.
He then married Katherine Schwarzenegger in June 2019, and they share three children together; Lyla, 6, Eloise, 4, and Ford, 1.

"It's an incredible blessing to be a father. It's also a lot of hard work. And so I think I just want to teach them that ... I don't know, I want to do my best," he told Fox News Digital in October. story: Michael Douglas discusses surviving stage 4 cancer, maintaining a lasting marriage and his close relationship with son Cameron. The Oscar winner has written a new memoir, "One Helluva Ride."

PARIS JACKSON SAYS DAD MICHAEL’S UNUSUAL RULE HELPED PROTECT HER CHILDHOOD

title: Jenny McCarthy living in a tent while battling ‘paranoid’ fears after mold poisoning diagnosis
summary: Jenny McCarthy says mold and mycotoxin poisoning left her living in a tent after two years of surgeries, infections and a desperate search for answers.
story: Donnie Wahlberg and Jenny McCarthy told Fox News Digital that they prefer ordering take-out and watching the faith-based TV show for date nights.
Jenny McCarthy's two-year health nightmare left her physically exhausted, emotionally shaken and so fearful of mold exposure that she traded her home for a tent in a desperate attempt to heal.
The former TV host revealed that her ordeal began in 2024 and spiraled into a series of painful infections, surgeries and unexplained symptoms during an episode of "The Jenny McCarthy Wahlberg Show."

"Okay, I have been dying to tell you this story because the last two years of my life have been absolutely fricking insane. Insane, okay?" McCarthy told her viewers. "Some of you guys already know that I’ve been dealing with mold and mycotoxin poisoning. I’ve talked about pieces of it before."
BRANDI GLANVILLE SPEAKS OUT ON COMPLEX DIAGNOSIS AND $6K MONTHLY MEDICAL BATTLE

Jenny McCarthy revealed she had been living in a tent after a grueling two-year health battle left her fearful of mold exposure and increasingly paranoid about her surroundings. (WireImage/Getty Images)
McCarthy claimed the whole ordeal began in 2024 with a toothache.

"And somehow that led me down a rabbit hole of doctors, surgeries, teeth being pulled, mysterious growths popping up in places you are not expecting, implants literally falling out, and eventually realizing my immune system was fighting something so much bigger," she said.
McCarthy's health spiraled into a series of medical complications, including severe dental infections, repeated surgeries, jawbone damage and recurring eye cysts.

The former "The View" co-host also battled debilitating leg cramps, facial swelling, worsening food allergies and insomnia before undergoing testing that she said revealed mold poisoning. McCarthy claimed the condition had compromised her body's ability to fight infections, leaving her physically and emotionally exhausted.

Her health nightmare began with a toothache in 2024 and spiraled into severe dental infections, multiple surgeries, jawbone damage, recurring eye cysts and other unexplained symptoms. (Kevin Mazur/Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for iHeartRadio)
"At one point, you know, I was just so desperate to heal that I literally was living in a tent," she revealed. "That’s right, living in a tent!"

After repeated procedures and inconclusive attempts to resolve her health problems, McCarthy said she experienced significant medical fatigue and became increasingly fearful of potential environmental triggers. She claimed she felt "like a freaking paranoid schizophrenic."
"I thought everything was poisoning me at this point, because look at me, I was a freaking hot mess, okay?"
McCarthy's functional medicine doctor eventually suggested testing her for mold after observing her repeated health problems. She initially dismissed the idea because she believed her home was clean.

Jenny McCarthy claimed testing revealed mold and mycotoxin poisoning, which she said compromised her immune system and contributed to her mounting health complications. (Michael Simon/Getty Images)
Around Christmas, she said the doctor contacted her urgently with test results indicating significant mold-related concerns.

"[My doctor] was like, ‘No, I need to talk to you now, you better get on the phone.’ So I get on the phone with her, and she says, ‘Jenny, you’ve got serious mold. You’ve got the type of mold that causes seizures. If this thing crosses the blood-brain barrier, I’m going to be talking to you in hospital. You’re going to start seizing,'" McCarthy recalled the doctor telling her.

McCarthy said she underwent an extensive treatment regimen after being diagnosed with what she described as mold and mycotoxin poisoning. Her protocol included daily infrared sauna sessions, numerous vitamins and supplements, a powdered drink, nasal spray treatments and lymphatic castor oil packs.

"I’m still in my mold detox, you guys," she revealed. "I’m still in it, like, I’m knee-deep in it. I’m in month seven of detox, and I’m too paranoid to honestly live anywhere else other than a tent."

title: Martha Stewart addresses backlash after dressing as homeless person for Halloween
summary: Martha Stewart says her deleted homeless Halloween costume was meant to bring awareness, but the backlash and online criticism only intensified.
story: Celebrity event designer Edward Perotti, known as the "King of Halloween," argues that Halloween has shifted from a celebration of personal expression and creativity into an over-commercialized, algorithm-driven spectacle. He criticizes retailers for pushing Halloween merchandise earlier every year and social media for encouraging clout-chasing displays, saying both trends diminish the holiday’s unique freedom from the obligations, gifts and elaborate meals associated with other celebrations. Perotti encourages people to reclaim Halloween by living in the moment, "shopping their home," creatively reusing old decorations and focusing on authentic self-expression and community rather than pre-packaged aesthetics.
Martha Stewart is addressing the backlash over her controversial Halloween costume, saying she intended to "bring more awareness" to homelessness.

The 85-year-old businesswoman and television personality sparked outrage after sharing — and later deleting — a photo of herself dressed in ripped jeans, a distressed button-down shirt, with a sign that read, "I AM HUNGRY. HELP ME!!"
The image was included in an Instagram carousel promoting Stewart’s QVC candles. The post was quickly removed after a wave of criticism flooded her comment section.
MARTHA STEWART QUESTIONS MEGHAN MARKLE’S HOMEMAKING CREDENTIALS WITH BLUNT CAREER ASSESSMENT
Martha Stewart's Halloween costume has sparked outrage online, with some dubbing the TV personality as "out of touch." (Getty Image; Martha Stewart Instagram)
Stewart later addressed the controversy in a statement to Page Six.

"I’ve spent decades teaching others how to celebrate Halloween — sharing fun, festive recipes, providing unique craft ideas, and giving tips on entertaining and hosting to make the most of one of my favorite holidays of the year," Stewart said.

"I am distressed that my Halloween costume yesterday, which was intended to bring more awareness to the very serious subject of homelessness, has offended people, which was never my intention," she continued.

"Homelessness continues to remain one of America’s greatest challenges and ongoing crises, something that I care deeply about and I have spent a significant amount of time and effort supporting charities that combat this ongoing social epidemic," Stewart added. "I am committed to continuing to make a difference."
Stewart claimed her costume was meant to "bring more awareness" to such a major issue.  (Katie Jones/WWD via Getty Images)
Despite Stewart’s explanation, the costume continued to spark criticism online.
"Definitely tasteless. Of all the things she could have done," one person wrote on X.
"Really? Is she that dense and misguided? You NEVER dress up as someone poor, sick or in dire circumstances. Never a fan but now disgusted," another person wrote.

"Just say that you’re sorry and you didn’t mean to upset anyone. It was just a poorly thought-out costume. Pretending that it was to raise awareness is just a very stupid lie," a critic wrote on Reddit.
"OMG, that’s the best she could come up with? Very lazy and condescending, thinking anyone would believe this explanation," another person added.
Social media users both criticized and defended the TV personality.  (Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for SKIMS)
Others defended Stewart and argued that people were taking the costume too seriously.
"Gawd … people are way too sensitive!" one person wrote.
Another user described the costume as being "in good fun" and wrote, "Leave her the f— alone."
"People are so thin-skinned. It’s Halloween and it’s a joke," another person wrote.
Stewart shared a statement to her Instagram page hours after addressing the controversy to Page Six.

She wrote in a note posted to her Instagram grid: "It's hard to admit when you've really screwed up. My earlier statement didn't go far enough. I know many people are suffering economically. Wearing a costume like I did was insensitive and not funny. I am very sorry. - Martha."

title: Candice Swanepoel: What to know about Tom Brady's rumored Victoria's Secret model girlfriend
summary: Sources say Candice Swanepoel and Tom Brady have been secretly dating for months in Miami, going to great lengths not to be spotted together.
story: Former New England Patriots player Jake Bequette and the ‘Outnumbered’ panel discuss the end of the Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen's marriage.
Supermodel Candice Swanepoel and Tom Brady have sparked romance rumors nearly two weeks after the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show.

"They both live in Miami, so it’s very convenient," the source added.
Candace Swanepoel and Tom Brady have been rumored to have been dating for several months. (Getty Images)

GISELE BUNDCHEN NOT BITTER AFTER UPSETTING TOM BRADY DIVORCE, GROOM CALLS BRIDE HER SISTER'S NAME & SAY WHAT?
Neither Brady nor Swanepoel have acknowledged the rumors publicly. Below is everything to know about Brady's new rumored girlfriend.
Candice Swanepoel walked the runway at the 2025 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show. (Gilbert Flores/Variety/Getty Images)
South African roots
Swanepoel was born in South Africa in 1988. She grew up on a dairy and beef farm in Mooi River – a small town in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.
Speaking about her upbringing, Swanepoel told V Magazine in 2023 one of her most "vivid" memories from childhood.
Candice Swanepoel in March 2026. (Getty Images)
"One of my most vivid memories as a child was seeing my father wake up at 4 am to take care of our farm. His dedication and drive is something that is now part of me," she said at the time.
Began modeling at 15
On her personal website, Swanepoel recalled the moment a talent scout saw her at a flea market when she was just 15.
"At the time, I was at St. Anne’s College, an all-girls boarding school where I embraced new friends and the potential of a great education," she wrote.
Candice Swanepoel models Tommy Hilfiger Spring 2006. (WireImage)
The following year, Swanepoel's life completely changed.

"Within a year of meeting the scout, at age 16, I was booking more and more modeling jobs all across Europe," she wrote. "While this was an incredible blessing for someone from such a sheltered upbringing, it also forced me to make tough decisions about my life at a young age."
Candice Swanepoel attends the 2009 Victoria's Secret fashion show after-party. (WireImage)
At 18, she spent a few years modeling in Paris, Milan, London and South Africa and decided to move to New York City to model full-time.

"Separated from everything familiar, I relied on my drive and ambition as I lived on my own overseas. I gave up a normal teenage life with my family and friends to pursue a dream, but what I have gotten in return is simply incredible," Swanepoel wrote.
A Victoria's Secret angel
Shortly after moving to New York, Swanepoel made her Victoria's Secret Fashion Show debut.
Candice Swanepoel walks the runway at the 2007 Victoria's Secret fashion. (Getty Images)

"I remember going to the casting for the show and being so nervous because I wanted it so badly," she told W Magazine in 2012. "And then once I was at the show—I took my mom with me, flew her from South Africa—I saw that kind of family vibe that they had. I’d been traveling alone for so long, and when I saw that, I said to my mom, ‘I want this so badly, I just want to be a part of something.’ Not just being alone in the fashion industry."

Candice Swanepoel and Joan Smalls have been friends for years. (Getty Images)

title: 'The Pitt' star Noah Wyle does 100 push-ups a day ‘come rain or come shine’ at 55
summary: Noah Wyle reveals his daily push-ups routine and chin-up bar goal with his accountability partner while filming the demanding medical drama "The Pitt."
story: The 55-year-old actor told Fox News Digital that he does 100 push ups every day on set and hopes to be able to do 10 pull ups by the end of season three.
Noah Wyle is sharing how he manages to stay fit while filming the hit medical drama, "The Pitt."

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 55-year-old actor shared what it means for the Cedar Sinai Board of Governors to honor the show with the Hollywood Leadership Award, and how he stays fit enough to keep up with filming the physically demanding HBO Max show.

"I have an accountability partner and a guy named Dash Land who's the on-set dresser and he and I do a hundred push-ups every day, come rain or come shine. That's the base," Wyle said about his fitness routine. "We try to add a little bit on top of that if we can, if we remember to. That's base. We also installed a chin-up bar recently. I have a goal to be, I'm going to embarrass myself, to do ten by the end of the season. I'm at six right now, solid six."
The actor stars in "The Pitt," an intense medical drama which follows emergency nurses and doctors over the course of one shift, with each episode showcasing one hour of a 12-hour shift.
Wyle shared he stays fit by doing 100 push-ups every day. (Warrick Page/HBO Max)
NOAH WYLE, MATT DAMON, LEONARDO DICAPRIO STILL CAPTIVATING AUDIENCES WELL INTO THEIR 50S

Wyle portrays Dr. Robby on the show, who is the chief attending physician and head of the emergency department at the fictional Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center, and is dealing with the emotional toll years of working on the frontlines of medicine can take on a person.

When speaking to Veja+ in January, Wyle said that the cast has to "take very good care of ourselves" almost "out of necessity," because while filming they "work 14 hours a day, five days a week, for nine months straight."
WATCH HERE: NOAH WYLE WORKS OUT EVERYDAY ON THE SET OF ‘THE PITT’ WITH AN ACCOUNTABILITY PARTNER

"At the beginning of filming I asked all the actors to do an exercise, and it was just standing on your feet for 15 hours," he said. "And as you stand, every hour begin to note where your fatigue is coming in – where do you get stiff, where's painful, when do you have to use the bathroom, when do you get hungry. Write all that down and then work it into the appropriate hour of your shift, and it'll give you the physicality that you need."

Men's Health referred this exercise as NEAT, which stands for non-exercise activity thermogenesis, which takes into account everyday activities which aren't necessarily considered exercise, but get the heart rate up, such as mowing the lawn or vacuuming the floor.

"My inspiration behind VADA itself, the name and everything was my grandmother," she told Fox News Digital.

title: Popular weight-loss drugs may prevent prediabetes from turning into diabetes
summary: A large study found GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide are linked to 41% lower all-cause mortality risk versus metformin in prediabetes.
story: Erin Palinski-Wade, a dietitian and diabetes educator, talks about important factors that affect blood sugar and gives an opinion on a recent study suggesting eating with a partner can decrease blood sugar levels.
Adults with prediabetes and obesity who took GLP-1-based medications had a 31% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes and a 41% lower risk of death compared with those taking metformin.

Metformin is an oral medication used primarily to treat type 2 diabetes, widely considered the first-line treatment, combined with lifestyle modifications. It is also sometimes prescribed to people with prediabetes to help prevent or delay progression.

The findings, which come from a large observational study, are set to be presented at the American Heart Association’s Scientific Sessions 2026 this weekend in Chicago. They have not yet undergone the full peer review process.
DR OZ LINKS OBESITY TO CHRONIC DISEASE SURGE, SAYS GLP-1S CAN 'JUMPSTART' BETTER HEALTH
The study involved health records for 256,492 adults with prediabetes and obesity, averaging 52 years of age.
Approximately half of the group received GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists) medications – including semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide and dulaglutide – and half received metformin.
Adults with prediabetes and obesity who took GLP-1-based medications had a 31% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes and a 41% lower risk of death compared with those taking metformin. (iStock)

Based on a three-year follow-up, in addition to the lower risk of diabetes and all-cause mortality, GLP-1–based medications were associated with 20% fewer strokes, 15% fewer heart attacks and 25% fewer cases of heart failure.

"The 41% lower risk of death from any cause surprised me most," study author Vinicius de Sousa Barzon Serra, M.D., a research fellow in the department of cardiovascular medicine at the Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale, Arizona, told Fox News Digital.

Approximately half of the group received GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists) medications – including semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide and dulaglutide – and half received metformin. (iStock)

"I expected GLP-1 medications to do better than metformin on blood sugar and diabetes risk, because they lead to much more weight loss. I was also struck that the benefit appeared across many outcomes, including heart attack, stroke, heart failure and atrial fibrillation."
POPULAR DIET SLASHES LIVER FAT BY 67% WHILE REVERSING PREDIABETES IN SOME PEOPLE

Nearly 40% of U.S. adults have prediabetes, according to statistics from the AHA. That condition is marked by blood sugar levels that are above normal but not yet elevated enough for a diabetes diagnosis.
As many as 10% of those with prediabetes will go on to develop type 2 diabetes each year.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Most earlier research on these medications focused on people who already had diabetes," Serra noted. "Our study suggests the prediabetes stage may be an important time to consider them, rather than waiting until they develop type 2 diabetes."

Nearly 40% of U.S. adults have prediabetes, according to statistics from the AHA. That condition is marked by blood sugar levels that are above normal but not yet elevated enough for a diabetes diagnosis. (iStock)
The study did have some limitations. While it found a link between GLP-1 medications and better health outcomes, it does not prove that the drugs were responsible.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
The findings are preliminary until published in a peer-reviewed journal, Serra noted.

"We matched patients by age, health conditions and other characteristics to make the groups comparable … even so, other differences between the groups may remain," he said. "We also grouped the GLP-1 medications together, so we could not tell whether individual drugs differ."

Metformin is an oral medication used primarily to treat type 2 diabetes, widely considered the first-line treatment, combined with lifestyle modifications. It is also sometimes prescribed to people with prediabetes to help prevent or delay progression. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

The study relied on patients' electronic health records, which may have contained missing or incorrect information. It is also possible that factors not measured in the study, such as medication dosage and compliance, could have influenced the results, the researchers noted.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
People with prediabetes and obesity should talk with their doctor about all their options and should not stop or change any medication on their own, Serra advised.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Metformin is a safe, inexpensive option with a long track record, and lifestyle changes such as healthy eating, regular physical activity and weight management remain the foundation of treatment," he emphasized to Fox News Digital.
"For some patients, a GLP-1 medication may be worth discussing, depending on their overall health, other medical conditions, cost and access. The decision should be made together with their doctor."

title: College students discover new muscle attachment that could improve hip surgery
summary: Two Tulane University sophomores found a previously unknown muscle in the hip during a cadaver lab session that even their professor couldn't identify.
story: Tulane University students Dominic Roy and Cooper Bruce join anatomist and professor Dr. Shane Tubbs to discuss their discovery of a previously undocumented pelvic muscle and what it could mean for medical research.
Two undergraduate students at Tulane University in New Orleans discovered an anatomical feature that even their professor couldn’t initially identify.
Dominic Roy and Cooper Bruce were both 19-year-old college sophomores at the time of the finding in 2024.

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Roy said it had been an ordinary day volunteering in the cadaver lab with R. Shane Tubbs, Ph.D., professor of neurosurgery and director of surgical anatomy at Tulane School of Medicine.
5 HABITS THAT COULD HELP KEEP YOU OUT OF A NURSING HOME, FROM AN ORTHOPEDIC SURGEON
The students were dissecting several specimens’ hips to compare where the iliacus joins the psoas major, a muscle that runs from the lower back through the pelvis to the upper thigh.
Front view of a woman's thigh and knee muscles with anatomical labels. (iStock)
When looking for a particular muscle, the iliocapsularis, which sits laterally in the hip, Roy found something else instead.
"I spotted a similar looking muscle that was on the other side of the Iliac fascia, close to the inguinal region of the pelvis," he said.
WEEKLY WEIGHTLIFTING SWEET SPOT MAY BE LINKED TO LONGER LIFE, STUDY FINDS
"I called Dr. Tubbs over and asked, ‘What is this?’ We didn't talk about this in our morning meetings ... and I think he was as stumped as me."
After searching through extensive literature and textbooks to see if the muscle had been previously identified, the team came up short, which suggested it was a new discovery.
The new muscle attachment discovered by Tulane undergrad students is illustrated in a diagram. (Tulane University/iStock)
"It was kind of like a reserved excitement," Bruce reflected. "Especially if the great R. Shane Tubbs can't put his finger on exactly what it is."
Physicians from overseas and rising medical school students also assisted with the discovery.
SIMPLE EXERCISE DONE JUST ONCE A WEEK COULD HELP LOWER BLOOD PRESSURE

"Everyone kind of huddled around the same specimen and we started draping and doing the pictures … I was in awe," Roy said. "I was like, ‘Oh, wow, this is happening so quick.’ It was seriously something special."
The findings were recently published in the journal Clinical Anatomy.
Tulane students Dominic Roy, left, and Cooper Bruce made a novel discovery while volunteering in the cadaver lab. (Dominic Roy)
Tubbs, who is also a co-editor-in-chief of the human anatomy reference textbook Gray's Anatomy, said Roy and Bruce’s discovery was "serendipity."
"[They] identified a different part of a muscle that we had not looked at yet," he confirmed to Fox News Digital. "It's deep in the pelvis and runs out to the front of your hip."
KNEE TREATMENT WITHOUT SURGERY OFFERS LASTING PAIN RELIEF FOR 80% OF ARTHRITIS PATIENTS, STUDY FINDS
Potential medical uses
Although the team has not yet determined the muscle’s function, clues suggest it may help stabilize the psoas major, a large muscle involved in bending the hip.
The next step is to determine whether MRI scans can reveal the muscle attachment, allowing researchers to study whether its presence is linked to more or fewer symptoms, according to the doctor.
Dr. Tubbs said his lab uses anatomical donors for education and research to identify clinical problems. (Tulane University)

"More research is needed for us to better elucidate what it does," Tubbs said. "Can you see it on imaging? Does it contribute to patients' problems? But I think this is the first step in identifying something."
As minimally invasive procedures become more common, Tubbs said awareness of this small muscle could improve care, particularly for patients undergoing hip surgery.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"They might use physical therapy to help rehab the muscle, because we did find that the fibers of this attachment directly attach into the front of the hip joint," he added. "So it may be that the muscle’s weak and causes symptoms, so you could rehab it."
Doctors could also use injections to weaken the new muscle if overactivity causes pain or other symptoms.
The muscle discovery could help improve future surgeries and hip pain, the professor said. (iStock)

"Surgeons are replacing hips and doing hip surgery on a daily basis, so if they see the muscle, potentially they could correlate the symptoms of the patient and whether or not maybe cutting the muscle would help the patient," Tubbs said.
Variations in anatomy
This muscle was not found in every cadaver, the researchers noted, as each human body is different.
"When you look beneath the layers of the skin, human beings have lots of variation," Tubbs said. "I tell our students that no two of you are built the same inside or out."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
The researchers found the same muscle attachment in gorillas, suggesting a possible evolutionary link.
Bruce said this raises the question of why this muscle would still be present in some humans and not others.
Tulane University School of Medicine is shown in New Orleans on Feb. 12, 2022. (iStock)
"Just by the nature of working with cadavers and not knowing a deep personal history of each individual … maybe this individual played soccer, or this person did a lot of rock climbing," he said.
"They might've had more need for this attachment ... It's difficult to make that connection."
Lessons beyond textbooks
Working with real cadavers has made a big difference in shaping future doctors, Tubbs shared, as the synthetic models that are now circulating in university labs are cookie-cutter.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Many people have the notion ... that the entire form of the human has been worked out, and we know all the different parts. And they think we've known that for hundreds of years," he said. "But in actuality, people are still discovering things about human anatomy."
Medical students "need to experience that variation" and have the hands-on experience before dealing with real patients, Roy commented.
Dr. Shane Tubbs poses in his office in the Murphy Building on Tulane's Downtown campus on March 27, 2026. (Kenny Lass / Tulane University)
Although the new muscle attachment will have to be studied across geographic regions, Tubbs said he expects the students' discovery will eventually be added to anatomical textbooks.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
The discovery inspired the students, now seniors, to further explore a career in medicine. Roy said he plans to enter a master’s program in anatomy.
"The bottom line is that anatomical discovery doesn't end when a textbook is published ... and discovery in the anatomical sciences continues on, even in the year 2026."
Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: NYC marathoner with 'heart for Jesus' remembered after tragic death for her faith, strength and charity
summary: Athlete Rachel Apa, 24, was running the NYC Marathon to honor her late grandfather and raise funds to fight Parkinson's disease when rhabdomyolysis struck.
story: Dr. Devi Nampiaparampil of the NYU Langone School of Medicine explains rhabdomyolysis warning signs after a runner dies two miles from the NYC marathon finish.
Rachel Apa, 24, died on Sunday, Nov. 1, while running the New York City Marathon after succumbing to complications from rhabdomyolysis, a rare muscle condition.

Apa made it to mile 24 – just 2.2 miles from the finish line – before collapsing. She received immediate medical attention and was taken to Mount Sinai Medical Center, where physicians worked to save her for more than six hours.
The athlete was declared dead at around 9:40 p.m., according to a report from The New York Times.
NYC MARATHON RUNNER, 24, DIES JUST 2 MILES FROM FINISH LINE AFTER SENDING DAD CHILLING TEXTS
Rhabdomyolysis causes the muscles to break down when over-exerted, which leads to muscle death, according to Cleveland Clinic.
When this disintegration occurs, toxic components of the muscle fibers can enter the circulatory system and kidneys, which can cause kidney damage, essentially acting as poison to the body.
Rachel Apa played Division I field hockey for Bucknell University. (Bucknell Athletics)

Apa graduated from Bucknell University, where she played Division I field hockey. Post-grad, she was a product manager for an electrical component company while also working on her MBA at Charleston Southern University (CSU).
In a tribute released Tuesday, the Christian university, where Apa began her graduate school education in August, said the CSU family "mourns the tragic loss."
HEALTHY ATHLETE HAD NO SYMPTOMS BEFORE MANDATORY HEART SCREENING REVEALED HIDDEN DEFECT

"Maxwell Rollins, assistant dean of graduate programs for the Nielsen College of Business, shared a recent class assignment where Apa stated her current mission was to take advantage of the talents and opportunities she had been blessed with to make an impact in any way she could in the lives of those around her," the statement reads.
Rachel Apa, 24, died while running the New York City Marathon on Nov. 1, 2026. (Instagram @rachelapa)

Rollins shared about Apa, "She wrote that her desire was to demonstrate Christ’s love and character in both business and everyday life. Though she had just started her MBA at CSU, her passion for others and heart for Jesus will continue to serve as an inspiration for all our students."

CSU president B. Keith Faulkner added, "The loss of a vibrant young woman in the prime of her life is a sorrow no parent can imagine enduring. The Charleston Southern family is surrounding the Apa family, along with all who knew and loved Rachel, with our prayers and support."
Apa’s former field hockey teams have mourned her loss in tributes posted to social media. (Bucknell Athletics)

"We will never fully understand why this happened to a young woman of such remarkable strength and character. Her final hours are forever marked by Rachel’s selfless dedication to helping others as she ran to raise funds in the fight against Parkinson’s disease."
MYSTERIOUS DISEASE SENDING YOUNG, HEALTHY TEXAS WORKERS INTO KIDNEY FAILURE

Faulkner continued, "We know that true peace comes only from the Lord, and we pray that His presence and comfort will be deeply felt by all who are grieving and by all whose lives were touched by Rachel’s extraordinary life and legacy."
Apa’s former field hockey teams also mourned her loss in tributes posted to social media.
Rachel Apa and teammate Kari Melberger celebrate with a hug during a field hockey match. (Bucknell Athletics)

Kristine Brown, vice president of strategic communications and marketing at Bucknell, shared a statement with Fox News Digital on Wednesday."Bucknell University extends its deepest sympathy for the family and friends of Rachel Apa '24 following her tragic passing while participating in Sunday's New York City Marathon," said Brown in the statement.
