Prosecutors are asking anyone with information about the investigation to contact the Cape May County Prosecutor's Office Special Victims Unit at 609-465-1135 or submit an anonymous tip at cmcpo.tips.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: Grocery store cyberattacks are ‘psychological warfare’ that could strike US, former FBI agent warns
summary: Former FBI agent Nicole Parker warns that hackers turning up supermarket freezer temperatures in Europe could target U.S. critical infrastructure next.
story: Former FBI special agent Nicole Parker says cyberattacks targeting grocery store refrigeration systems in Europe underscore the need to protect critical infrastructure.

Former FBI Special Agent Nicole Parker warned that the next attack on Americans’ sense of security could come through the grocery aisle after suspected hackers have turned up supermarket freezer temperatures in Europe and fueled fears that everyday necessities could become weapons of "psychological warfare."
Parker warned that cyberattacks targeting the systems people rely on for food and other essentials could also strike the United States.
"Every human being has to eat," Parker told Fox News Digital. "This is the grocery store."
HACKERS COULD ALREADY BE INSIDE AMERICAN UTILITIES, CYBER EXPERTS WARN OF 'TROJAN HORSE' THREAT
Cyberattacks on supermarkets could target the U.S., according to a former FBI agent.  (iStock)

Her warning comes as the Army Criminal Investigation Division’s Cyber Field Office works with the Defense Commissary Agency and the Defense Criminal Investigative Service to determine what caused refrigeration failures at military commissaries in August, an Army CID spokesperson confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Investigators are also working with French law enforcement as they examine whether the U.S. failures could be linked to refrigeration outages in Europe. A cyberattack has not been established as the cause of the military commissary malfunctions.
MAJOR US GROCERY CHAINS HIT BY CYBERSECURITY INCIDENT
U.S. Army Fort Huachuca in August said an outage affected the base's commissaries. (U.S. Army Fort Huachuca)
At least six commissaries, grocery stores on military bases serving military personnel, experienced refrigeration problems in late August.
"ALL frozen food has spoiled," Fort Huachuca in Arizona said in an Aug. 26 Facebook post.
FOREIGN HACKERS BREACH TWO MORE US WATER UTILITIES, THREATEN SAFETY OF COLORADO RESIDENTS

Other affected locations included F.E. Warren Air Force Base in Wyoming, Naval Station Newport in Rhode Island, Columbus Air Force Base in Mississippi and Travis Air Force Base and Fort Irwin in California. Fort Irwin limited commissary sales to dry goods after its malfunction.
In at least one case, refrigeration units were set to higher temperatures overnight rather than simply shutting off, Reuters reported.
HOW FOREIGN HACKERS COULD 'CRUMBLE' AMERICA BY TARGETING ONE ESSENTIAL UTILITY

U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. Drew Jordan Pocaigue, a supply chain manager with Headquarters and Support Battalion, Marine Corps Installations West, loads a broken refrigerator onto a truck during Operation Clean Sweep II at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, Calif., April 3, 2025.  (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Cpl. Noah Martinez)

Separately, refrigeration systems at European supermarkets were disrupted Monday, forcing some retailers to discard food. Reuters reported that affected businesses included stores in Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg, with temperatures in some systems reaching 122 degrees Fahrenheit.
Parker said the incidents underscore a threat she has long discussed with former FBI colleagues: cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure.
AMERICA'S NEXT WAR COULD REACH US SOIL, TOP ARMY GENERAL WARNS
"What we're seeing right now is in Europe and other places, but it can very well happen on our soil," she said.
She described the danger as "asymmetrical warfare" in which an attacker can disrupt daily life without firing a missile or sending troops onto a battlefield.
AN AI CYBERATTACK COULD TURN OFF AMERICA'S LIGHTS BEFORE WASHINGTON EVEN UNDERSTANDS WHY
A young woman carries a shopping basket filled with fresh produce while shopping in a grocery store. (iStock)
"No one in law enforcement underestimates the harm that could be caused by a cyberattack against our country or against our allies," Parker said.
The identity of those behind the European incidents remained unknown, Reuters reported Wednesday. Parker also cautioned against drawing conclusions about who was responsible.
UKRAINE SAYS AIR ALERT SYSTEM HACKED AFTER FALSE RADIATION WARNING IN KYIV
"Again, we don't know who did this," she said.
For Parker, the potential damage goes beyond spoiled food. Targeting a basic necessity can also shake the public’s sense of security.
IF HACKERS CRIPPLE AMERICA'S WATER, THE CONSEQUENCES COULD BE CATASTROPHIC
"This asymmetrical warfare has a very strong psychological impact, but we're Americans. We will not falter ever," she said.

Parker said the response must extend beyond investigators tracking down hackers. Elected officials and local leaders responsible for keeping communities running need training and plans to help residents if essential services are disrupted.
"We're in a place now where it's not just enough for law enforcement to be prepared," she said.

City managers, mayors and city council members must understand potential threats and how they would take care of their communities, Parker said. She stressed the need to identify vulnerabilities and stop attacks before they happen.
Parker urged families to keep basic supplies on hand and have a plan in case a cyberattack disrupts essential services.
"I think if you are prepared, you do not have to fear," Parker said.

She encouraged Americans to keep food, water and needed medicine on hand, gather important documents in a designated location and talk about how family members would communicate during a power outage. She also suggested having a battery-operated AM radio.
"I'm not saying that, you know, you need to go buy everything off of the shelves," Parker said.
Instead, she urged people to think about practical preparations as they go about their routines.

For Parker, who lives in Florida, the approach is familiar.
"We're used to hurricanes," she said. "The preparation would be very much the same."

title: Four dead, including Washington deputy, following domestic call shooting; another deputy on life support
summary: A Spokane County sheriff's deputy died and another is on life support after a SWAT team was ambushed responding to a domestic violence call.
story: A Spokane County sheriff's deputy was killed and another remains on life support after a gunman ambushed SWAT officers responding to a domestic violence call in Washington state (Credit: KHQ).
A Washington state sheriff's deputy has died and another remains on life support after they were ambushed while responding to a domestic violence call that turned deadly, authorities said Wednesday.
Spokane County Sheriff's Office deputies responded to a home Tuesday after a woman ran to a neighbor's house reporting that her brother had shot her, FOX 13 Seattle reported.
Responding officers learned the suspect had an active felony arrest warrant and had access to multiple guns and additional victims could be inside the home.
NYPD OFFICER SHOT, GUNMAN KILLED AFTER ARMED BARRICADED STANDOFF IN BROOKLYN: POLICE

A Spokane County Sheriff's deputy walks to a hospital where two SWAT officers were taken upon being shot during a domestic violence response call. One deputy was killed and another remains on life support but is not expected to survive. (Fox News)
The Spokane County Sheriff's Office deployed a SWAT team to assist at the home. As SWAT officers approached the house, a gunman opened fire from inside.
"SWAT team members and deputies approached the house, attempted to breach the door and were met with gunfire," Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels said during a news conference.
PHILADELPHIA POLICE OFFICER KILLED, PARTNER SHOT 12 TIMES IN AMBUSH; SUSPECT FOUND HIDING IN TREE
The entrance to a hospital where two Spokane County sheriff's deputies were taken after being shot Tuesday. (Fox News)

Deputies returned fire and pulled the two wounded deputies to safety. Both deputies were rushed to a hospital along with the initial female victim who was treated for injuries that were not life-threatening.

Inside the home, investigators found one person dead, while another body was found in the yard. The suspect was also found dead on the property. Authorities have not released the identities of those who died.
PHILLY OFFICER MURDERED IN LINE OF DUTY PROMOTED TO SERGEANT AS POLICE FROM AROUND US ATTEND HIS FUNERAL
On Wednesday, the sheriff's office confirmed that one of the wounded deputies succumbed to his injuries. He is survived by his wife and two children.
"Although we know our deputies knew the risks, they bravely moved toward danger to protect others they did not know," the sheriff's office said in a statement.
"They did this with honor and with an unwavering sense of duty to their oath to serve and protect the citizens of Spokane County; they heroically placed themselves in mortal danger."
The second deputy remains on life support but is not expected to survive, according to officials.
INDIANA SHERIFF'S DEPUTY SHOT THREE TIMES IN HOSPITAL ER AFTER STOPPING TO HELP STRANDED MOTORIST
A helicopter hovers in Spokane, Wash. (Fox News)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"As an organ donor, arrangements are being made, and he will continue to serve others with the gift of life," the agency added.

title: 911 call captures hero dad’s bravery before he took down Oregon elementary school gunman
summary: Newly released 911 audio captures Kaylub Giamanco's desperate call before he rushed into Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, with a gun.
story: Newly released 911 audio captures the call from Kaylub Giamanco, the hero dad who took down a gunman at Oregon’s Silver Rail Elementary School. (Credit: Deschutes County District Attorneys office)

An Oregon father who rushed into his daughters' elementary school and shot a gunman made a desperate vow in newly released 911 audio, telling a dispatcher, "I have a gun, and I will shoot them right now."
Kaylub Giamanco’s call captures the urgency outside Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend on Oct. 15, before the armed father intervened to stop an attack that killed three children and a teacher.
"Oh my god. Hello 911. Someone’s at the school. My daughter’s school with a gun," Giamanco says in the recording released by the Deschutes 911 Service District.
DEMOCRATS CALL FOR GUN CONTROL AFTER OREGON SCHOOL SHOOTER REPORTEDLY USES SHOTGUN PURCHASED BY HIS MOTHER
Kaylub Giamanco returns to his home in Bend, Oregon, Oct. 17, 2026. Giamanco is the man who took down a school shooter at Silver Rail Elementary School. (Kevin Perkins for Fox News Digital)
The dispatcher urges him to wait for police.
"OK, tell me exactly what happened. Don’t do anything. Let me get an officer there, OK?" the dispatcher responds. "OK, I understand. Stay on the line with me."
OREGON TEACHER WHO WRESTLED SHOTGUN FROM SCHOOL GUNMAN SHARES EMOTIONAL MESSAGE AFTER ATTACK
Police tape is placed outside Silver Rail Elementary school, where a shooting took place, on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026 in Bend, Oregon. (Joe Kline/AP Photo)
As the call continues, voices can be heard discussing where the attacker is and whether he is firing.
"They’re on the south side, entering the building, right now," Giamanco says, before warning that people are being shot.
DEMOCRATS' LATEST GUN-CONTROL PUSH RUNS INTO INCONVENIENT FACT ABOUT HOW SCHOOL KILLER WAS STOPPED
Police tape is placed outside Silver Rail Elementary school, where a shooting took place, on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. (Joe Kline/AP Photo)
"Sir, I need you to tell me what’s going on. We have help en route," the dispatcher says.
Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter whose two daughters attended the school, later told Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB) he feared he would not survive going inside.
THE ONE LESSON EVERY PARENT SHOULD TEACH THEIR CHILD AFTER THE BEND SCHOOL SHOOTING
School buses are lined up outside Silver Rail Elementary school, where a shooting took place, on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. (Joe Kline/AP Photo)

"That’s when I started hearing children pleading for their lives, and then I started hearing gunfire. And I just started army crawling faster and faster, and I told myself this is probably the last thing that I’m ever going to do," he told the outlet.

Giamanco entered the school with a .40-caliber pistol he legally kept in his vehicle and found a teacher struggling with the 16-year-old attacker, Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said during an Oct. 16 news conference.
The teacher had thrown her cellphone at the gunman and tackled him before Giamanco shot him multiple times, according to the chief.
OREGON TEACHER WHO WRESTLED SHOTGUN FROM SCHOOL GUNMAN SHARES EMOTIONAL MESSAGE AFTER ATTACK
Three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert were killed. A child and another teacher were wounded, police said.
For Giamanco, praise for stopping the gunman has come alongside anguish over those he could not save.
BEND SCHOOL DISTRICT HONORS SLAIN TEACHER, PRAISES STAFF MEMBER'S COURAGE DURING ATTACK: ‘FOREVER GRATEFUL’
"I want to apologize for not saving their babies," he told OPB. "The gratitude for saving people’s children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn’t save."
Lambert’s family praised the father’s intervention in a statement read during the October news conference.
"We want the bystander who intervened to know we know he is going through a rough time, but we are grateful, and we think he is a hero," the family said.

title: Man allegedly held teen captive in basement, forced her to remove braces with pliers after Snapchat meeting
summary: Kylie Arellano was allegedly forced to remove her braces with pliers and confined to a basement for over 500 days before her rescue in Oregon.
story: Missing Utah teen Kylie Arellano has been found safe in Oregon after a 500-day search.

The missing Utah teenager found alive in Oregon nearly 18 months after her disappearance was allegedly beaten repeatedly and forced to remove her braces with pliers to hide her identity, according to disturbing new details in the case.
Kylie Arellano, now 17, vanished from Garden City, Utah, on May 29, 2025, when she was 15. Federal authorities have now charged a 39-year-old man in her alleged captivity.

In court documents reviewed by Fox News Digital, Adam Hunter Harmel allegedly became "very violent and aggressive, often hitting" the teen and further forced her to remove her braces with pliers so that she could not be identified.
MISSING UTAH TEEN KYLIE ARELLANO FOUND SAFE IN OREGON AFTER 500-DAY SEARCH
Kylie Arellano was reported missing May 30, 2025. (Rich County Sheriff's Office/Facebook)
The federal complaint also paints a chilling picture of captivity inside Harmel's home, where Harmel allegedly confined the teenager to the basement, where the two shared a bed.
To prevent her from escaping, the complaint says, Harmel also "kept a knife under his pillow and made MV [minor victim] sleep against the wall."

Investigators said Harmel had expressed a desire to start a family with the teenager, stated that he was interested in minors and repeatedly sexually assaulted her in 2025 and 2026, according to the complaint.
Harmel allegedly transported Arellano across state lines with the intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.
12-YEAR-OLD NORTH CAROLINA GIRL ESCAPES ALLEGED KIDNAPPER AFTER BEING FORCED INTO TRUCK
The teen helped spark her own rescue by revealing her identity to another player she met on the online game "Among Us," authorities said. (Rich County Sheriff's Office/Facebook)
The criminal complaint, filed Nov. 2 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah, also outlines a timeline of alleged grooming, isolation and abuse.
For more than 500 days, Arellano's mother held out hope after finding her daughter's jacket discarded in the driveway and her phone turned off.
That wait ended Nov. 1, when law enforcement rescued the teenager from a home in Oregon following a tip from the parent of another player of the online game "Among Us."

According to an affidavit written by FBI Special Agent Andrea Elder, Arellano's family first reported in 2025 that she had been groomed online, with communications beginning on gaming platforms before moving to other social media apps.
According to a law enforcement source, the suspect allegedly met the teenager on Snapchat before her disappearance.

During the investigation, the FBI also learned that Arellano was allegedly groomed on platforms that are often used by Nihilistic Violent Extremist (NVE) Groups members to solicit sexually explicit photos and maiming photos, according to a release issued by the Department of Justice (DOJ).
JILLIAN MICHAELS URGES PARENTS TO FIGHT BACK AGAINST BIG TECH'S 'ADDICTIVE' GRIP ON KIDS
Kylie Arellano, now 17, vanished from Garden City, Utah, when she was just 15. (Rich County Sheriff's Office/Facebook)
Authorities allege that, in May 2025, Harmel met the teenager online, claimed he had a disability involving his "messed up" hips and offered her money to travel to Oregon.

Harmel drove from Oregon to Perry, Utah, to pick her up on or about May 29, 2025. Immediately after she entered the vehicle, according to the complaint, Harmel threw her phone into a river in Logan Canyon, drove her to his home in Huntington, Oregon, and told her she was not allowed to leave.

A housemate living at the home told the FBI that Harmel claimed he had brought home a "new girlfriend" from Utah. The housemate did not see the teenager until about two months after her arrival, when she ran back into the basement.
According to the complaint, Harmel provided Arellano with a phone that lacked cellular data capabilities, limiting her internet access to Wi-Fi.
Her path to freedom began in mid-October 2026, when she connected with another minor while playing "Among Us."

After moving their conversation to another social media app, Arellano revealed her real identity and told the minor she was being held against her will at a man's home in Oregon. She also said she thought police were no longer looking for her.
FRANCE BECOMES FIRST EU NATION TO BAN SOCIAL MEDIA FOR CHILDREN UNDER 15
A knife from inside the home where Kylie Arellano was held in Oregon. (FBI)
Her mother contacted the FBI, which monitored a Nov. 1 video call with Arellano during which she showed investigators the knife Harmel kept and other evidence corroborating her claims.
That same day, Oregon State Police and federal agents rescued the teenager and took her for medical treatment.
A search of Harmel's residence uncovered knives, BB guns and sexual lubricant, according to the complaint. Harmel was arrested during a traffic stop in Ontario, Oregon.
Harmel was scheduled to make his initial appearance in federal court Wednesday.
In a statement, U.S. Attorney for the District of Utah Melissa Holyoak said the priority in the case was the "safe return of the minor victim."
"Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
FBI Director Kash Patel issued a similar warning to those who target and exploit children.

"The FBI and our partners are coming for you. We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice, and protect America’s most vulnerable," he said.

title: Helicopter crash near Miami leaves at least 1 dead, 2 injured: report
summary: At least one person was killed and two others were seriously injured after a helicopter crashed near Nixon Beach off Key Biscayne, Florida. Investigators are examining the crash.
story: At least one person is believed dead and two others were rescued after a helicopter crashed into the water near Miami, Florida, on Wednesday, according to a local report. (Credit: WSVN)
A helicopter crashed in the waters off Miami on Wednesday, killing at least one person and seriously injuring two others, officials confirmed.
The small helicopter went down near Nixon Beach, off Key Biscayne, Florida, shortly after 11 a.m., WSVN reported.
The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said the crash occurred near Bill Baggs State Park.
The U.S. Coast Guard confirmed that one of the three people aboard the helicopter died, while the other two were taken to a trauma center, according to The Associated Press.
Miami-Dade Fire Rescue crews responded to the scene, where two people were rescued from the water, the report said.
TWO HELICOPTERS COLLIDE NEAR MOUNT EVEREST DURING RESCUE FLIGHT, KILLING ONE, INJURING OTHERS
Rescue boats and divers were also seen in the water near helicopter wreckage in Miami on Wednesday. (WSVN)
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said preliminary information indicated the Robinson R44 II helicopter appeared to have been conducting a photography flight when it crashed.

"A total of three patients were reported," authorities said, according to NBC Miami. "Two adult trauma alert patients were transported by ground rescue units from the City of Miami Fire Rescue and Key Biscayne Fire Rescue to a designated landing zone, where MDFR Air Rescue transported them to the main trauma center."
Aerial footage from the scene showed the helicopter's yellow emergency floats in the water near a Miami-Dade Fire Rescue boat off the 1200 block of Crandon Boulevard.
PILOT'S PUSH TO LEVEL JET MAY HAVE TORN OFF KEY PIECE FOUND MILES FROM FLORIDA CRASH, FORMER NTSB EXPERT SAYS
Aerial footage from the scene showed the helicopter's yellow emergency floats in the water as rescue divers swim nearby. (WSVN)
Divers were also seen in the water near the wreckage.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Officials did not immediately identify the three people aboard the helicopter.
The cause of the crash remains under investigation.
This is a developing news story; check back for updates.

title: Armed security guard hailed as hero after fatally shooting gunman at massive Tampa Citibank site
summary: Florida authorities on Wednesday confirmed a suspect and one victim are dead following a reported active shooter situation at a Tampa-area business park.
story: The Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office gave an update on a gunman who drove onto Tampa Citibank Center property and allegedly opened fire Wednesday afternoon.

An armed security guard was hailed as a hero by authorities Wednesday after engaging a gunman who drove onto the busy Citibank Center property in Tampa, Florida, fatally shot a woman, and then opened fire inside the building's cafeteria.

The suspect crashed into an outdoor seating area where multiple people were eating lunch just after 12 p.m. upon driving through a fence at the Sabal Park Office Development, Frank Losat, a chief deputy with the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office, told reporters at the scene. The gunman then got out of his vehicle with a rifle and fatally shot a woman.

An armed security guard employed by Citibank shot the suspect inside a nearby building's cafeteria during a gunfire exchange, authorities said. The gunman was taken to Tampa General Hospital where he later died.
"The security guard that's employed by Citibank stopped the threat," Losat said. "Was there a potential for further violence? Absolutely. So kudos to that security guard and the people they employ."
Four people were also treated at a local hospital for injuries that were not life-threatening. It is unclear where the victims were wounded during the incident.
SHOOTING AFTER MAGIC CITY CLASSIC IN ALABAMA LEAVES 1 DEAD, 8 INJURED
Authorities at a Tampa-area business park where an active shooter was reported Wednesday, resulting in one suspect and one victim dead.  (Fox News)
Officials said deputies with the sheriff's office responded to the scene within minutes of the reported shooting.
At the time the chaotic scene broke out, there were 3,200 Citibank employees on the property, Losat said. Another 367 law enforcement personnel responded to the scene.

"With that being said, with that many witnesses… we will be doing interviews well into the night," Losat said. "The crime scene is very large. Remember, we have an outdoor scene. We have an indoor scene. Our crime scene will be processing the scene, which will take several hours, if not until tomorrow."

Losat did not release the name of the suspected gunman or the victim, pending notification to the next of kin. Investigators are still trying to determine a motive for the attack. Authorities have cleared the Citibank property.
FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SHOOTING LEAVES 12 INJURED, INCLUDING 6 CHILDREN, NEAR FOOTBALL STADIUM
Authorities staged near the Citibank Center campus in Brandon, Florida.  (Fox News)
Nearby Hillsborough College encouraged students and staff to shelter in place at the time of the incident. The FBI and ATF have also responded.
The scene showed adults with children moving away from the business campus, which has a daycare center, affiliate FOX 13 Tampa Bay reported.
"We are aware of an incident impacting our site in Tampa, Florida and are coordinating with law enforcement," Citibank said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Citibank employees were asked to meet at the triage area in the parking lot of the Sheraton Tampa Brandon Hotel. Families of employees were instructed to meet at the reunification site at Staybridge Suites Tampa East.
A Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office van at the Citibank Center business area.  ( Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Citibank Center serves as the banking giant's regional data processing and communications hub, according to the developer's website. The campus is composed of four 130,000-square-foot three-story office buildings, and a 138,000-square-foot amenities building.

The campus has roughly 25,000 employees and offers amenities such as dining services, a gym, child care facilities, a bank branch and shops including a drug store, dry cleaner, hairdresser and shoe repair shop.

"The low-rise campus is surrounded by lushly landscaped berms with outdoor plazas, fountains, and waterfalls to provide a secluded, tranquil environment," the website states. "Each building is interconnected by enclosed walkways to ensure personnel comfort and building security as well as provide a homogenous atmosphere among the individual buildings and associated staff."
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

title: Pilots' push to level jet may have torn off key piece found miles from Florida crash, former NTSB expert says
summary: NTSB investigators found the Learjet 60's left tail elevator scattered up to 3.8 miles from the Florida crash site, pointing to an in-flight breakup.
story: Former NTSB investigator Greg Feith joins 'Fox & Friends' to analyze the deadly Palm Beach plane crash after debris was found miles from the crash site. Feith discusses how ice and severe turbulence may have impacted the loss of control.
Federal investigators found a key piece of the private jet that crashed in Florida on Sunday broken apart and scattered miles from where the plane went down.

The Learjet 60 took off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport around 10:37 a.m., headed for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. Just before 1 p.m., it went down in Palm Beach County, killing everyone aboard.
Investigators recovered a part that controls the plane's pitch in three separate pieces, one of them nearly four miles from where the Learjet 60 went down.
NTSB FINDS 'NO EVIDENCE' OF MAR-A-LAGO CONNECTION AFTER FLORIDA JET CRASH KILLS NINE PEOPLE
Investigators work at the scene of a plane crash in Greenacres, Fla., on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)
Investigators recovered the left tail elevator, a "very important piece of evidence," National Transportation Safety Board member Thomas B. Chapman told reporters Tuesday.

Chapman said that pieces of the left tail elevator were found anywhere from 1.3 to 3.8 miles away from the crash site, explaining that it likely separated from the plane before crashing. Investigators will study it to determine whether losing the part helped bring the plane down or whether forces acting on the aircraft tore it loose.
FORMER NFL STAR SAYS HE PREVIOUSLY FLEW ON PRIVATE JET THAT CRASHED IN FLORIDA: 'ABSOLUTELY DEVASTATED'
Investigators hope to have access to the crater by Wednesday, which is currently blocked off and being worked on by public utility crews.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB
A Learjet 60 slammed into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday afternoon, erupting into a massive fireball just nine miles from Mar-a-Lago. (Aki Kuusisto via Storyful)

Former NTSB investigator Greg Feith told Fox News that the debris points to an in-flight breakup, possibly caused by one of the pilot's efforts to try and level the jet and over-stressing its structure.
SEND US A TIP

"One of the clues here is that there was an in-flight breakup and that a critical flight control, as the board member said, did come off in flight," said Feith. "You can see that the airplane leveled off at about 8,000 feet for a very short period of time. That may have been one of the pilots trying to control the airplane, level the airplane, and in doing so over-stretched the structure of the aircraft, causing those parts to fail and come off."
FLORIDA PLANE CRASH VICTIMS IDENTIFIED AFTER 9 PEOPLE KILLED IN FIERY WRECK

Adam Robinson, 45, an Austin tech entrepreneur, was among nine people killed in the Nov. 1 Learjet crash in Palm Beach County, Florida. Robinson was traveling with his wife and their two young children. (Fox News)
"They're close to the main impact, which says that those parts came off at a very low altitude," he added.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Austin tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, 45, his wife, Helen Sharp, 40, and their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, were among the nine people killed, along with the children's nanny, Anita Maria Cetina, and couple Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr, according to their families. The plane's captain, Jeff Gregory, 55, and copilot Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, 20, also died.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Adam Robinson and his wife, Helen Sharp, were traveling with their two young children when the Learjet carrying them from Texas to the Bahamas crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Nov. 1. (Fox News)

Weather conditions have been identified by federal investigators as a "major focus" of the probe, after the crew reported icing and moderate turbulence at approximately 35,000 feet shortly before the aircraft experienced a rapid loss of altitude.

The jet was equipped with a cockpit voice recorder, but investigators haven't found it and can't yet confirm it was on board when the plane went down, NTSB officials said.

title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Tyler Robinson blames Trump post in push for camera ban
summary: Tyler Robinson's lawyers cite Trump's Truth Social post slamming the judge as they renew efforts to block cameras from the Charlie Kirk case hearing.
story: Utah prosecutors propose a January 2028 trial start for the murder of Charlie Kirk, while the defense team for Tyler Robinson requests a delay until 2029. 'Outnumbered' panelists weigh in.

Accused Charlie Kirk assassin Tyler Robinson's attorneys are again asking a Utah judge to block cameras from an upcoming hearing, this time arguing that President Donald Trump's online post elevates a risk of prejudicing the potential jury pool against their client.

The 23-year-old Robinson's lawyers have routinely objected to the presence of news cameras in the courtroom and failed to convince the judge to block them. They've targeted both still photography and video cameras.
With Robinson due back in court next week, they seized on a presidential Truth Social post from late October.
TRUMP SAYS JUDGE IS 'DESECRATING' CHARLIE KIRK'S MEMORY AMID FIGHT OVER ASSASSINATION TRIAL DATE

Attorneys for accused assassin Tyler Robinson, right, are asking a Utah judge to block news cameras from covering his next hearing — arguing that a post from President Donald Trump on Truth Social increases the potential "prejudicial impact" of electronic media coverage. (Brendan Smialowski/AFP via Getty Images; Rick Egan/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool)

"The judge in the Charlie Kirk case is doing a terrible job!" Trump wrote after Robinson's lawyer proposed a trial date in the third quarter of 2029. "This case should be tried within a month, not three years — and it should be over with! The judge is desecrating the memory of the Great Charlie Kirk, while taking forever to ask questions that people already know the answer to. The whole Country is mocking him and our 'Legal' System. JUSTICE FOR CHARLIE!"

In addition to reiterating a standing objection to the court's procedure for challenging cameras, Robinson's lawyers again claimed that "continuing [electronic media coverage] threatens Mr. Robinson's rights to a fair trial by an impartial jury by perpetuating bias in the public against Mr. Robinson."
TYLER ROBINSON'S LAWYERS SEEK CAMERA BAN FOR SEPT. 1 HEARING, SAY CASE IS NOT A 'REALITY TV SHOW'

Charlie Kirk throws hats to the crowd after arriving at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025, in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

"The President’s post only heightens the prejudicial impact of EMC at the November 9 hearing," they wrote, claiming that cameras "create an unnecessary risk" that statements made in court can spread without context.

"Such out-of-context statements provide unnecessary ammunition for public commentary, including by politicians, that risks exerting undue pressure on the proceedings," they added. "Even still photography creates risks of prejudicial dissemination and out-of-context interpretation."
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
A map of the UVU campus shows key locations surrounding the courtyard where Charlie Kirk was shot and killed on Sept. 10, 2025. (After-Action report for Utah Valley University)
Robinson's lawyers noted that the upcoming scheduling hearing will not include any presentation of evidence or witness testimony.
"Any resultant scheduling order will be publicly accessible, and the proceeding will remain open to the public and members of the press, who may attend and report on it," they wrote.
SEND US A TIP
People run after shots were fired during an appearance by Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

And although there are no witnesses expected to testify next week, Robinson's lawyers also renewed their objection to cameras "because this Court's procedure for adjudicating the request does not allow any opportunity for witnesses to address privacy or security concerns."

Read the filing:
ERIKA KIRK RIPS 'ABSURD' 2029 TRIAL TIMELINE FOR CHARLIE KIRK'S ALLEGED ASSASSIN
Robinson is accused of assassinating the 31-year-old Kirk at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025, during a Turning Point USA event at Utah Valley University in Orem.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Utah County prosecutors had floated Jan. 31, 2028, as their preferred trial date but said they could be ready in October 2027. Robinson's defense team has proposed late 2029 as a "soft target" trial date.

title: Teen previously convicted in shooting accused of killing pregnant mom of 4 inside Spirit Halloween
summary: Monte Smith, 17, allegedly opened fire inside a Spirit Halloween store at Solano Town Center, killing pregnant mother Constance Hages and wounding six.
story: One person was killed, and six others wounded in a shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, California. At least three victims are in critical condition.

A California teen released after a prior shooting arrest is now accused of gunning down a pregnant mother of four at a Spirit Halloween store, prompting prosecutors to push to try the 17-year-old as an adult.
Monte Smith was arrested Nov. 2 after the attack at Fairfield’s Solano Town Center left Constance Hages, 31, dead and six others wounded, according to Fairfield police.
The Solano County District Attorney’s Office has also charged him with two counts of murder and asked a judge to move his case to adult court.
CALIFORNIA GUNMAN REPEATEDLY RELEASED BEFORE DEADLY RAMPAGE, FIERY SHOOTOUT WITH DEPUTIES
One person is dead after a shooting Friday night at a California Spirit Halloween store. (KOVR)

Smith had already been arrested in another shooting before the deadly attack at Spirit Halloween, according to Fairfield police. That case involved gunfire in a local high school parking lot after school hours in 2025. He received a sentence and was later released, the department said.

"It’s time for change in California," Fairfield Police Chief Dan Marshall said, according to KTVU. "I don’t know how many more people have to die at the hands of youth. Hopefully we’ve had plenty enough."
MARYLAND MAN ACCUSED OF GIRL'S FATAL SHOOTING RELEASED FROM PRISON DAYS BEFORE
Constance Hages leaves behind four children, according to a GoFundMe organized by her aunt. The 31-year-old was killed in the Fairfield Spirit Halloween shooting. (GoFundMe)
Prosecutors also pointed to Smith’s record in explaining why they want him kept in custody.
"Due to the seriousness of these crimes, the minor’s criminal record, and the threat to public safety, the people will argue that Smith remain detained," the DA’s office said.
TWO TEEN SUSPECTS HELD AFTER 5 FAMILY MEMBERS KILLED IN 'TARGETED MASS SHOOTING'
The filing also alleges a prior violent offense conviction, described as a strike, though the DA’s announcement did not specify the underlying offense.
Hages’ death has left four children without their mother, according to a GoFundMe organized by her aunt, Clanisha Morton. Police confirmed Hages was pregnant when she was killed.
"Constance was deeply loved, and her absence has created an overwhelming void in the lives of everyone who knew and cherished her," Morton wrote.
The family is raising money for funeral expenses and care for her children.
15-YEAR-OLD ACCUSED OF FIRING INTO CROWD DURING DEADLY SEATTLE MASS SHOOTING CLAIMS SELF-DEFENSE
"Constance was deeply loved," her aunt, Clanisha Morton, wrote in a fundraiser for Hages’ family after the deadly Spirit Halloween shooting. (GoFundMe)
The gunfire erupted around 8:30 p.m. Oct. 30, after Smith allegedly walked into the store and spotted another customer whom investigators believe he intended to target, police said.
He pulled out a gun and fired multiple rounds, striking that person and six others, according to police. Hages died at the scene.
Investigators have not identified the intended target or said what led to the shooting.
Smith fled within minutes, just as officers arrived, police said. As first responders treated the wounded, a school resource officer helped investigators identify the suspect.

The officer recognized Smith as a former student while reviewing surveillance video from the store and immediately alerted detectives, according to police. That recognition helped identify him within hours of the initial 911 call, and detectives ultimately located him at a residence in neighboring Suisun City.
Police initially withheld Smith’s name because of his age. The DA’s office later publicly identified him in its charging announcement.
CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL GRADUATION SHOOTING KILLS TEEN, INJURES CHILD AND TWO OTHERS
Six surviving victims were taken to hospitals, and at least three were in critical condition, according to officials. (KOVR)
The FBI also assisted with the investigation, confirming to Fox News Digital that its Evidence Response Team helped Fairfield police process a portion of the crime scene.

In addition to the two murder counts, Smith faces three counts of attempted murder, three counts of assault with a semiautomatic weapon and multiple gun enhancements, according to the DA’s office. Prosecutors also filed a multiple-murder special circumstance allegation.
The office announced that Smith’s arraignment and detention hearing was scheduled for Nov. 4 at 9 a.m. Its request to prosecute him as an adult requires a judge’s approval.
Police have not identified the school involved in the earlier shooting or said when Smith was released in that case.

In an update Saturday about the surviving victims, police said a 16-year-old boy, a 19-year-old man and a 32-year-old man were in critical condition, while a 23-year-old man was in critical but stable condition. Two other men, ages 19 and 43, had been treated for gunshot wounds and released.
The department’s arrest announcement did not provide updated conditions.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"Although an arrest has been made, our work is not over," Fairfield police said. "The criminal justice process will now move forward, and we remain committed to ensuring accountability for the lives impacted by this senseless act of violence."
Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to contact Fairfield police at 707-428-7600 or email 1030mall@fairfield.ca.gov.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Man, 86, and his dog rescued hundreds of miles off California coast after going silent for 2 months
summary: A Coast Guard aircrew spotted the sailboat 460 miles off San Diego after an emergency beacon alert launched a dramatic search and rescue mission.
story: An 86-year-old man and his dog were rescued from a disabled sailboat drifting hundreds of miles off the California coast after he had not been heard from for more than two months.
An 86-year-old man and his dog were rescued from a disabled sailboat drifting hundreds of miles off the California coast after he had not been heard from for more than two months.
The man was sailing from Astoria, Oregon, to Pago Pago, American Samoa, when contact with him was lost Aug. 20, the U.S. Coast Guard announced Friday.
Authorities were alerted Oct. 24 that he was overdue, launching a search for him and his sailboat, the Willow Wind.
TRAGEDY AT SEA LEAVES TEEN STRANDED ON OVERTURNED BOAT FOR NEARLY 3 DAYS IN FRIGID WATERS
An 86-year-old man and his dog were rescued hundreds of miles off the California coast after he had not been heard from for more than two months. (U.S. Coast Guard)
Three days later, the Coast Guard received an emergency beacon alert from the boat and sent aircraft and a cutter to search the area. Nearby ships were also asked to assist.

"Watchstanders coordinated the launch of a Coast Guard Air Station Sacramento C-27 Spartan aircrew and diverted an HC-130 Hercules aircrew and the Coast Guard Cutter Robert Ward (WPC 1130), and requested assistance from nearby vessels," the Coast Guard said.
A Coast Guard aircrew spotted the Willow Wind that evening about 460 miles off San Diego.
The motor vessel Grand Orion reached the sailboat early the next morning, but rough seas initially made it too dangerous to rescue the man and his dog.
TEEN BOATER FOUND CLINGING TO CAPSIZED VESSEL AFTER 3 GO MISSING; 2 BODIES RECOVERED
The following morning, a Coast Guard helicopter crew picked up the man and his dog from the Grand Orion about 170 miles west of Ventura, California. (iStock)
Later that day, the Grand Orion crew was able to safely bring them aboard. The Willow Wind had damaged sails and was left drifting at sea.
The following morning, a Coast Guard helicopter crew picked up the man and his dog from the Grand Orion about 170 miles west of Ventura, California.
They were flown to San Diego, where the man was taken to Scripps Mercy Hospital for further evaluation.
The Coast Guard did not provide additional details about his condition.
CRUISE VACATION TAKES FRIGHTENING TURN AS PASSENGER IS AIRLIFTED FROM SHIP
A Coast Guard aircrew spotted the Willow Wind about 460 miles off San Diego.
"We are grateful to the merchant mariners and Coast Guard crews whose coordinated efforts brought this search to a successful conclusion," Coast Guard Cmdr. Jason Nguyen said in a statement.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"This case highlights the importance of carrying emergency communication equipment and creating a float plan, so someone ashore knows your voyage plans."
The Coast Guard could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.

She graduated with a journalism degree in 2021 from the University of Hawaii at Manoa. Story tips can be sent to sophia.compton@fox.com.

title: Christa Pike asks court not to send her to former prison block following failed execution
summary: Christa Pike claims her life is in danger if moved back to her former housing unit, citing severe weakness after surviving the botched lethal injection.
story: If surviving attempted lethal injections on Sept. 30 left her mentally impaired, Christa Pike could be spared from the death penalty, according to a leading scholar on capital punishment in the U.S., who also breaks down some other possibilities.

Christa Pike, the death row inmate who survived a botched lethal injection attempt, has filed an emergency federal court motion to stop prison officials from transferring her back to her former housing block, claiming her life is in danger.
Pike, 50, is currently in solitary confinement in the infirmary at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville as she recovers from the execution attempt.
In her court filing, Pike argued that her severe physical weakness leaves her vulnerable and unable to protect herself if returned to her previous unit, the New York Post reported.
CHRISTA PIKE'S EXECUTION DOCTOR SAYS MISPLACED IV SENT LETHAL DRUGS INTO HER ARMS INSTEAD OF VEINS

An execution gurney is shown alongside a Tennessee Department of Correction booking photo of death row inmate Christa Pike, who has filed an emergency federal court motion to stop prison officials from transferring her back to her former housing block. (Greg Smith/Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images; Tennessee Department of Correction via AP)

"This pod houses inmates with significant histories of assaults and disciplinary problems," the motion states. "In my two years living in this pod… I witnessed multiple assaults by close custody inmates of other inmates and guards, multiple individuals who were undergoing acute psychological breakdowns, and significant danger."
Pike emphasized her inability to handle potential threats.

"In my current physical condition, I could not defend myself or get away if another inmate attacked me," she wrote. "I am afraid that I will be seriously hurt if I am moved to that pod while I am this weak."
CHRISTA PIKE DISCHARGED FROM HOSPITAL, RETURNED TO PRISON AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION, ATTORNEYS SAY
Christa Gail Pike appears remotely from Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation for her hearing in Knox County Criminal Court in Knoxville, Tenn., on Aug. 11, 2026. (USA Today Network via Reuters Connect)

The motion further states that returning to her prior housing unit poses a "high risk of infection and further injury" due to unsanitary conditions, specifically noting that she would be forced to clean and use an alleged "roach-infested shower" on her own while still recovering, according to the Post.

Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow participant in a Job Corps training program in Knoxville. In 2001, she received an additional conviction for the attempted murder of another inmate.
DEATH ROW KILLER CHRISTA PIKE DESCRIBES WAKING UP AFTER EXECUTION SHE NEVER EXPECTED TO SURVIVE

Poised to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than two centuries, Pike survived after two doses of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital failed to kill her during the Sept. 30 execution attempt.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Following the failed procedure, Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee issued a temporary halt on all executions pending an investigation.
Fox News Digital has reached out to the Tennessee Department of Correction.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Melania Trump hails Oleshky ceasefire as potential ‘spark’ for progress amid Ukraine-Russia war
summary: Melania Trump called the Oleshky ceasefire "a spark in a world of darkness" as Russian and Ukrainian envoys praised the deal at a rare White House event.
story: The 'Outnumbered' panel discusses Melania Trump's diplomatic efforts, including brokering a temporary limited ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.

First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House on Thursday, hailing the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region as a potential "spark" for peace that lasts beyond a temporary regional ceasefire.

"We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said in a White House trilateral news conference with the two warring countries. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark."
"Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire," she added, calling Oleshky "a spark in a world of darkness capable of illuminating the best in humanity."
INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL

Trump said she became aware of a humanitarian crisis in the region in September and directed her representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on her behalf. She said both countries agreed to work with her as an "exclusive intermediary" to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region, deliver humanitarian aid and create a safe evacuation route for civilians.
Her remarks were followed by comments from Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who said Russian President Vladimir Putin appreciated President Donald Trump’s efforts to stop the fighting.
US WILL MEDIATE UPCOMING UKRAINE-RUSSIA TALKS IN ABU DHABI, WITKOFF SAYS

Leader of the Servant of the People political party of Ukraine, David Arakhamia, sitting side by side with Russia's presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev was a unique image at first lady Melania Trump's remarks on the ceasefire in Oleshky at the White House in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 5, 2026. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)

"President Putin also appreciates President Trump's peacemaking effort and his team working on a peace plan to resolve Ukrainian crisis," Dmitriev said in a rare moment of a Russian diplomat speaking at the White House. "President Trump has asked President Putin to support a number of initiatives on exchanging of prisoners, on releasing U.S. prisoners on humanitarian efforts. And President Putin supported those ideas and those initiatives."

"And it's very important that cooperation between Russia and Ukraine and Russia in the United States matters not only for our two nations, but for the entire world," he continued. "Let us continue making great humanitarian contributions. We can together, let us build a future of peace, partnership and prosperity for the benefit of our families, our children and future generations."
RUSSIA RELEASES AMERICAN TEACHER IMPRISONED ON UKRAINE MERCENARY CHARGES AFTER TRUMP PRESSED PUTIN

First lady Melania Trump, left, and civilians being evacuated from Oleshky, Ukraine, in October 2022 during the early days of the Russia-Ukraine war. (Umit Bektas/Reuters; Alexander Ermochenko/Reuters)
"Dear Melania, you saved and touched so many lives," he concluded.
David Arakhamia, the leader of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's political party, called Melania Trump's ceasefire the 'biggest de-escalation since 2022," when the war began.
UKRAINE'S ZELENSKYY OPEN TO FREEZING FRONT LINES IN CEASEFIRE WITH RUSSIA

"Madam first lady, I would like to thank you: You did an amazing job," he said. "I think when everything started with you and your team, we had about 5% of people who believed in success, and 95% of skeptics who said it wasn’t going to work. Now, after it happened, it’s switched completely: 95% of the people believe that we can do things like that, and 5% are still skeptical."
Peace is now a matter of when, not if, he added.
KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE
Signature page from Oleshky ceasefire agreement. (Provided to Fox News Digital)

Getting fearful Ukrainians out of the Russian-controlled city is an important step toward deciding how peace will be made and determining the long-term fate of the occupied territory of southern Ukraine.

"On the first day, people in the area did not believe it was happening," Arakhamia said. "They stayed in their homes, waiting to see if the clock was ticking backward. The next day, they started walking around their homes. The day after that, they came to see their broken homes and find their belongings.

"This is really emotional to watch and supervise, to understand what we are doing," he added. "I think we are creating momentum where both sides are learning the little mechanics of how to keep the peace when the peace comes.
"I would also like to sincerely thank you, from my heart, for doing this."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Dmitriev attended the event and met with U.S. officials, sources told Reuters. Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, also attended the event.

title: Protests erupt across France after left-wing groups call for mobilization
summary: An estimated 270,000 people joined nationwide strikes and protests across France on Thursday, putting pressure on President Emmanuel Macron's government.
story: Fox News foreign correspondent Jeff Paul reports on nationwide protests in France, where up to 700,000 demonstrators are expected and 70,000 police officers have been deployed. The U.S. embassy is warning Americans about possible danger in traveling.
France deployed 70,000 police officers Thursday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets for nationwide strikes and protests after left-wing groups called for a mobilization.
In Paris, the Eiffel Tower was closed; in Lyon, French riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters; and near Toulouse, a high school was set on fire, according to Reuters.
"We need to turn up in big numbers on the streets today," the news agency quoted the head of the left-wing CGT union Sophie Binet as saying.
The demonstrations come after France was rocked by violent protests in October, which outgoing French President Emmanuel Macron blamed on "ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic."
FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC'

A car burns as demonstrators look on during a nationwide day of strikes and protests over wages, the cost of living and public services, called by French labor unions and joined by high school and university students calling for better education conditions, in Lyon, France, on Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
An official close to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that by early Thursday, around 270,000 people had joined the union action in 180 rallies outside the capital.
About a third of France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate, some because of student blockades and others because teachers were on strike, The Associated Press reported.
Toby Harris, an Australian tourist who was visiting Paris on Thursday, told Fox News Digital that "I feel like it's probably a good thing that there's like political action in the city.
"So if things have to be closed, because people want to make a point, then I'm sort of all for it," she added.

Ashley Bradshaw, a tourist from Utah, said outside the Eiffel Tower that "we were going to go tour the opera today and because of the strike, we couldn't access that which was a bummer, but we're happy that we get to just be here in Paris."

French high school students, officials and protesters face off with French riot police as they block a street with garbage bins during high school blockades ahead of a demonstration in Paris on Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
Nuñez said the 70,000 police officers being deployed are backed by armored vehicles, drones and helicopters.
Authorities in the western region of Brittany also said "masked individuals" tried to block roads in Rennes, while some committed "serious acts of violence," including throwing steel balls at police.
AMERICANS WARNED OF VIOLENT PROTESTS AS MAJOR TOURIST DESTINATION FACES SHUTDOWN THREAT
Protesters carry a banner and Communist flags during a nationwide day of strikes and protests in Lyon, France, on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
France’s main unions warned that the country is on the brink of recession and that layoff plans are multiplying.
"Fuel, food products, rent, gas, electricity... everything’s going up except wages and pensions," they said in a joint statement, according to The Associated Press.
Riot police detain a protester during a protest in Lyon, France, on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Laurent Cipriani/AP)

The U.S. Embassy had issued an urgent security alert for Americans in France ahead of the demonstrations, warning travelers to brace for severe disruptions, sudden curfews and the potential for violence.
The rallies come as the campaign to succeed Macron as president next May heats up, with political parties seeking to capitalize on the movement.
A member of the French gendarmerie shoots a tear gas canister during a demonstration in Nantes, France, on Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Macron is constitutionally barred from seeking a third consecutive term, while far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the favorite to win, the AP reported.
Fox News Digital's Kelly McGreal and The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Multiple flights in Europe diverted because of bomb threats
summary: At least 11 planes from cities, including Dublin, Madrid, and Warsaw, were diverted or grounded over bomb threats that have been determined to be unfounded.
story: Fox News foreign correspondent Jeff Paul reports on a series of bomb threats forcing multiple commercial flights to divert or make emergency landings across Europe. Paul details incidents involving Aer Lingus, Finnair and Wizz Air flights alongside previous security warnings that government authorities classified as hoaxes.
Multiple planes across Europe were diverted and forced to make emergency landings Thursday because of bomb threats that have turned out to be unfounded.
At least 11 planes, originating from cities including Copenhagen, Dublin, Helsinki, Madrid, Milan and Warsaw, have been affected. The source of the threats was not immediately clear.
These incidents came after several flights in Europe received similar warnings on Tuesday that the U.K. government described as "malicious hoax threats."

"Upon receiving a threat regarding the placement of an improvised explosive device on board 4 aircraft heading to Prague, we are preparing with colleagues from Prague Airport for their landing. We assess the relevance of the threats as low," Czech Police wrote on X, before adding that inspections of the planes yielded "negative results."
The threats come at a time when European officials have been blaming Russia and Iran for "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage, which both Moscow and Tehran deny, Reuters reported.
RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT

A Ryanair plane sits at Sofia Airport after flights from Copenhagen and Madrid landed there, according to the Bulgarian interior minister, as bomb threats forced unplanned landings across Europe on Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)

Earlier, a flight from Dublin to Rome was diverted to a military air base in western France because of a bomb threat, according to French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu’s office. That flight landed safely at the base in Evreux in Normandy, with all 151 passengers and six crew members disembarking, the office said.
A LOT Polish Airlines flight from Warsaw to Brussels landed at its destination, where inspections found no hazardous or suspicious items, the airline said.
A Wizz Air flight from Milan to Bucharest landed safely in Bucharest following a bomb threat, according to airport spokesperson Teo Postelnicu.
FRENCH SUPERMARKETS FACE MILLIONS IN LOSSES AFTER CYBERATTACK HITS REFRIGERATORS NATIONWIDE

A police officer and a sniffer dog inspect a Ryanair airplane and its baggage after Ryanair's operations center reported a bomb threat received during a flight from Manchester to Murcia, according to Guardia Civil, in Murcia, Spain, on Nov. 3, 2026. (Reuters)
Finnair said that Flight 1761 from Helsinki to Rome was targeted by a bomb threat, but nothing was found after it landed in the Italian capital.
Three Ryanair flights bound for Sofia, Bulgaria, had to make emergency landings because of bomb threats on board.

A Finnair aircraft sits on the tarmac at Fiumicino Airport in Fiumicino, near Rome, Italy, on Nov. 5, 2026, after a Finnair flight from Helsinki was escorted to its scheduled landing by Italian Air Force jets following bomb threats that forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe. (Reuters)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Two of the flights — one from Copenhagen, Denmark, and the other from Madrid — landed safely at Sofia’s Vasil Levski Airport, airport officials told reporters. The third Sofia-bound flight, from London’s Stansted Airport to Sofia, had been diverted and landed safely at the airport in Plovdiv, Bulgaria’s second-largest city, Plovdiv Airport CEO Krassimir Peshev said.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: US Marine dies in training incident at Japan military base, officials say
summary: A U.S. Marine with the 3rd Marine Division died during a training exercise at Camp Schwab in Okinawa, and the incident remains under investigation.
story: A U.S. Marine died following a training incident on a military base in Okinawa, Japan. (Yuichi YAMAZAKI / AFP via Getty Images)
A U.S. Marine died Tuesday after an incident during training at Camp Schwab in Okinawa, Japan, military officials said.
The incident happened in Okinawa, on a Marine Corps base near the northeastern coast of Okinawa Prefecture.
The Marine, who was identified as Lance Cpl. Devin J. Hernandez, 25, of Maryland, was with the 3rd Marine Division.
ALLEGED KILLING BY MARINE PROMPTS US MILITARY TO RESTRICT OFF-BASE LIBERTY IN OKINAWA

"It is with heavy hearts that 3rd Marine Division announces the death of a Marine following a training incident at Camp Schwab, Okinawa, Japan, on Nov. 3, 2026," the 3rd Marine Division said in a statement to ABC News. "We express our deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of our Marine."

Hernandez was participating in fast-rope training at Camp Schwab when he sustained injuries during the training, the 3rd Marine Division said in a later statement to Fox News Digital. He was transported to a hospital and later succumbed to his injuries.
The Marine's death remains under investigation, the 3rd Marine Division said.
The Marine's death remains under investigation. (Getty Images)

"The Marines and Sailors of 3rd Marine Division mourn the loss of one of our own. We extend our deepest condolences to Lance Cpl. Hernandez’s family, friends, and fellow Marines. Our focus remains on supporting them while we fully investigate the circumstances of this tragic incident," Maj. Gen. Kyle Ellison, commanding general of the 3rd Marine Division, said in a statement.
Lt. Tyler Thomas, a spokesperson for the III Marine Expeditionary Force, declined to tell ABC News whether anyone else was injured.
MARINE MISSING FROM USS ANCHORAGE NOW FOCUS OF RECOVERY MISSION OFF CALIFORNIA COAST
The Marine was identified as Lance Cpl. Devin J. Hernandez, 25, of Maryland. (Yuichi YAMAZAKI / AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Roughly 50,000 U.S. troops are stationed in Japan, with most based on Okinawa. The island remained under U.S. control from the end of World War II until 1972.

Currently, nearly 80,000 Americans live on Okinawa, including about 30,000 active-duty service members from all four military branches, with the Marine Corps accounting for the largest presence there.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Canadian mother and daughter dead after suspected grizzly bear attack on hiking trail
summary: Jennifer Balcarras and Selah Reed went missing on a hiking trail minutes from their Bella Coola home before a suspected grizzly bear attack.
story: Captain Carter Brown, an Alaskan fishing guide, shares his experience after a grizzly bear swam directly up to his boat in Soldotna, Alaska, on ‘The Story.’
A Canadian woman and her daughter were killed in a suspected grizzly bear attack over the weekend while hiking on a trail near their home, according to authorities.

Jennifer Balcarras, 48, an art therapist, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, went missing Saturday after going for a walk on the Snooka West Trail, just minutes from their home in Bella Coola, British Columbia.
Loved ones grew concerned when Balcarras failed to show up for a scheduled online meet-up on Saturday, her brother, Matt Balcarras, told The Vancouver Sun.
Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her 20-year-old daughter, Selah Reed, were killed in a suspected grizzly bear attack.  (Facebook/Josh Kara Balcarras)
A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO NOT GETTING MAULED BY A BEAR WHILE HIKING OR CAMPING THIS SUMMER
After failing to reach the pair, relatives asked the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) for a welfare check on Sunday morning.
Authorities discovered Balcarras' vehicle parked at the trailhead. Her body was recovered Monday, and search teams found Reed's body on Tuesday.

A Grizzly bear in Jasper National Park, Canada. A Canadian woman and her daughter were killed in a suspected bear attack in British Columbia over the weekend, conservation officials said. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)
GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL
"There was evidence to suggest a bear may have been involved," Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the British Columbia Conservation Officer Service, said in a video update posted to social media.
Tyre noted that officers were actively working to "locate and capture any bears involved" and said it was not immediately clear if more than one animal was responsible.
HIDDEN DANGER AT POPULAR US NATIONAL PARK FORCES TRAIL CLOSURES AS BEAR SIGHTINGS CLIMB

"Any captured bear will be assessed," conservation officials added in a statement. "If it is determined to have been involved in the attack, it will be dispatched in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety."
Matt Balcarras expressed shock over the location of the attack, emphasizing that his sister and niece were experienced in the region.
"They were not naive city folks," he said. "They were strong women living the life."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The tragic encounter came less than a year after a grizzly bear injured 11 people, including fourth- and fifth-grade students, during a school field trip near Bella Coola.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Bukele warns Haitian gang leaders that his forces will 'finish' them as he did in El Salvador
summary: Video shows Salvadoran attack helicopters repelling gang fighters in Croix-des-Bouquets as Nayib Bukele escalates military operations in Haiti.
story: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele says his troops will rescue four missing technicians by force if Haitian gangs refuse to hand them over. (Reuters.)

After crushing powerful criminal gangs in El Salvador, President Nayib Bukele has turned his attention to the Caribbean nation of Haiti, deploying 2,000 troops after four Salvadoran military aviation technicians disappeared following an Oct.18 ambush near Port-au-Prince.

"We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too," Bukele wrote in a message on X directed at Haiti's criminal groups. Bukele stressed that the operation's objective was not to invade Haiti or conduct a long-term occupation, but to recover the four missing Salvadorans alive.
The disappearance has become a national priority for Bukele, who has warned Haitian gang leaders that El Salvador is prepared to use overwhelming force if the men are not returned alive.
FLORIDA JURY CONVICTS 4 MEN WHO PLOTTED ASSASSINATION OF HAITI'S PRESIDENT FROM SOUTH FLORIDA HUB

In a screen grab taken from a video released Oct. 29, 2026, soldiers walk across the airport tarmac to board an aircraft after El Salvador's deployment of thousands of troops to Haiti, days after four Salvadoran members of a U.N.-backed force went missing in a gang ambush, in Comalapa, El Salvador. (Handout via Reuters)

The aviation technicians were assigned to a medical unit as part of the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) in Haiti when their armored vehicle was attacked in Croix-des-Bouquets. Haiti’s National Police announced Tuesday, more than two weeks after the attack, that it had found the charred remains of the vehicle in the Santo neighborhood of Croix-des-Bouquets. Police said, however, they found no sign of the missing men.
El Salvador says the men were abducted, the Haitian government says the soldiers are missing, and one gang leader says they are dead.

In a post on X Tuesday, directed at the "Haitian people" and written in Haitian creole, Bukele recalled the 1806 assassination of Jean-Jacques Dessalines, who proclaimed Haiti’s independence from France in 1804 and who many regard as the founder of Haiti.
"Dessalines liberated Haiti, but some people who were by his side betrayed him and killed him," Bukele said. "Those traitors still exist in Haiti."
SUSPECTS IN HAITIAN PRESIDENT'S ASSASSINATION TRANSFERRED TO MIAMI, ACCUSED OF FUNDING PLOT WITH COVID FRAUD

Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele joined the annual National Prayer Breakfast in Washington, D.C., warning attendees that violent gang members in his country have a documented history of worshiping Satan. (Alex Pena/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Bukele also reposted video of a helicopter engagement in Croix-des-Bouquets.
"Gangs were attacking GSF soldiers from Chad," he wrote. "We arrived quickly and repelled the attackers with our attack helicopters."
Bukele has the backing of President Donald Trump, who, when asked by reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Halloween, confirmed speaking with the Salvadoran president.
"He said that he has a big problem with Haiti," Trump said. "They killed some of his people. I said, 'You're running your country. You have to do what you have to do.'"
Unlike previous foreign interventions, Bukele's deployment has the backing of Haiti's transitional government.
"The international force is not here to replace the state," Haitian Prime Minister Didier Fils-Aimé said Tuesday in his first remarks about the deployment. "They're here to support us."
Fils-Aimé added that Bukele "understands our fight. … He came to stand on the side of the Haitian people."
‘DONROE’ DOCTRINE AND CONSERVATIVE VICTORIES SQUEEZE CARTELS IN LATIN AMERICA

An armored personnel carrier of Haiti's U.N.-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) patrols an area after El Salvador announced a rescue mission for four air force members in the GSF who went missing after a gang ambush in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, Oct. 23, 2026.  (Patrice Noel/Reuters)

The operation has drawn criticism from human-rights advocates and gang leaders who warn that a military escalation could worsen civilian suffering. The U.N. says at least 5,700 people have been killed or injured due to the gang violence in Haiti since Jan. 1 as security forces struggle to contain the violence.
The U.N. has also indicated that El Salvador’s deployment is separate from the GSF and has warned El Salvador must follow applicable international law.

One of those gang leaders is Wilson Joseph, known as "Lanmò Sanjou," leader of the powerful 400 Mawozo gang. He accused rival gang Chen Mechan of carrying out the ambush and claimed the Salvadorans are dead, he told The Associated Press.

Joseph also sent a letter to United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres asking the U.N. for mediation and warning Bukele's "vengeful remarks, expectations, and threats … will lead to an escalation of violence and a logic of reprisals, of which the Haitian people would be the first victims."
EXCLUSIVE: HAITIAN ILLEGAL ALIEN GANG MEMBER WHO WENT VIRAL YELLING ‘BIDEN FOREVER’ DURING ICE ARREST DEPORTED
An armed member of the G9 and Family gang patrols a roadblock in the Delmas 6 neighborhood of Port-au-Prince, Haiti, March 11.  (AP Photo/Odelyn Joseph)

Joseph was indicted by the U.S. in 2022 on hostage-taking charges related to the 2021 kidnapping of 17 missionaries, including 16 Americans, and remains the subject of a reward of up to $1 million for his arrest.

Bukele dismissed such appeals, accusing gang leaders of attempting to use civilians and international concerns about human rights as a shield to preserve their power and avoid accountability. Bukele has said that negotiations have only prolonged the crisis that has devastated Haiti for years.

After years as one of the world's most violent countries, dominated by powerful gangs including MS-13, El Salvador launched an unprecedented crackdown in 2022 under a state of emergency. Authorities carried out tens of thousands of arrests, ultimately detaining more than 90,000 suspected gang members.

Supporters credit the strategy with driving homicide rates to historic lows and restoring public safety. Critics accuse Bukele's government of human-rights abuses, arbitrary detentions and erosion of due-process protections.

Salvadoran soldiers return to a base after El Salvador deployed thousands of troops to Haiti in response to four Salvadoran members of a UN-backed force that went missing in a gang ambush, in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, Oct. 30, 2026.  (Patrice Noel/Reuters)

The question now is whether that model can be exported to Haiti, where gangs control large portions of Port-au-Prince and wield influence over key transportation routes and neighborhoods. Despite years of international intervention, security conditions have continued to deteriorate.

The GSF has struggled with manpower shortages and operational limitations, operating below its Security Council-approved intended strength, leaving Haiti's government unable to reassert full control over much of the capital.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"We can help you defeat them, but we are not your enemies," Bukele wrote on Tuesday. "We must stand up, take back control of our communities, and put under our control those who are making us endure all this pain, all this suffering. We are right there beside you… Haiti will be free."
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Tyler Speicher is an American journalist living in Slovenia after spending 25 years covering stories ranging from the Little League World Series to hurricanes, 9/11 and its aftermath for New York City news outlets, including 20 years on the Fox News Channel assignment desk.

title: Netanyahu faces coalition showdown as rivals maneuver to form Israel's next government
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu faces a critical test as President Isaac Herzog decides who will receive the mandate to form Israel's next government.
story: Fox News senior White House correspondent Jacqui Heinrich joins ‘America Reports’ to report on President Donald Trump’s announcement that the U.S. will halt aid to Israel at the end of the year and his closing push as midterm voting gets underway.

TEL AVIV, Israel: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s hold on power in Israel will be tested Wednesday as President Isaac Herzog begins consultations with leaders of all parties elected to the 26th Knesset before deciding which lawmaker to task with forming the next government.

The final vote count, published last Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee, gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for the opposition alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot — 61 seats are needed to form a government.

On Monday, Netanyahu posted to X that "the public in Israel does not want a government that depends on Ra'am and the Joint List—parties that support terrorism and reject the existence of the Jewish state."
NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks to the audience at a conference in Jerusalem, Sunday, July 27, 2025. (AP Photo/Ohad Zwigenberg)

"A clear majority in the Jewish public chose the Likud as the largest party and me, as prime minister, to lead the next government. We aspire to form a broad government with our partners and with any party that wishes to do so and does not support terrorism. I am open to holding discussions on the matter," he added.

The two predominantly Arab parties he pointed his criticism at are the Joint List and Ra'am who secured a historic combined total of 19 seats, potentially positioning them as kingmakers in the government formation process.

A Joint List source told Fox News Digital that the alliance is likely to endorse Eisenkot to be the first lawmaker tasked with forming a government. If both predominantly Arab parties were to back him, he would receive recommendations from parties representing more than the 61 seats needed.
The lawmaker tasked with forming a government will have 28 days to do so, with the president authorized to grant an extension of up to 14 additional days.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog during an interview with Fox News Digital in Jerusalem, Israel. (Yoav Dudkevitch/TPS-IL for Fox News Digital)
Consultations will be held in ascending order of seat count, beginning with Religious Zionism-Zehut and Shas, which each won six seats, followed by Yisrael Beiteinu, which secured seven.

On Thursday, Herzog will meet with the leaders of United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit, which each won seven seats, followed by The Democrats and Ra'am, which each won eight, the Joint List (11), BeYachad (12), Yashar (21) and Likud (27).

Defense and government affairs commentator Amir Oren told Fox News Digital that while Herzog is formally free to choose whom to task with forming a government, he would be inclined to select the candidate whose nomination is backed by parties representing a majority of Knesset seats.
FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE
"He must then task Eisenkot with forming the next government. That does not mean Eisenkot will succeed. If he fails, he will have to return the mandate to the president," Oren said.

Eisenkot may, in fact, struggle to assemble a 61-seat governing coalition, given competing interests within the opposition bloc.
